# Tester guide

This guide is enough to test Mapping by hand without knowing the project: where to get the app, what the computer needs, how the app saves, where each control is, how to report, and the test scripts, each step with the **action** and the **expected result** that can be seen on screen or on disk.

## Start here

Mapping is a web app to mark rectangular areas on images, organize them into layers and annotate them, saving everything in a `mapping.json` next to the images. The app makes no network request: nothing you do leaves the computer.

**For whoever tests by hand:** read sections 1 to 5, skip section 6 if you will not use the MCP server with Claude Code, run the test scripts in the order of the table below and report in the template of section 10. Appendix A is not for you; appendix B has the disk commands that R6 and R7 ask for.

Without the MCP, do only step 2 of section 6 from row 4 (the test repository and the folders, without the `mapping-mcp.js`), run R3.1 to R3.5 and skip R3.6, R3.21, R3.23 and R5, marking them "not executed (no MCP)". The main scripts (R0 to R43) are made for the cloud agent to run **alone**. The **on-demand scripts (manual)**, today RP, RF, RA, RB and RT, are not part of the full round or the directed one: they run apart, in an on-demand session, only when the owner asks (end of section 8). The dependencies between the scripts are at the start of section 8. Section 9 (advanced manual testing) is a script of its own, after a full round without high or medium findings.

What this guide **does not** test: whether a panel is easy to find or whether a text is clear to someone who has not read the documentation. That is left to people, in real use.

Whoever tests through an agent (the Claude Code session in the cloud) starts with [`docs/TESTING-NUVEM.md`](TESTING-NUVEM.md) and reads this guide together with appendix A.

## 1. Where to get the app

| Option | Address or source | What it implies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Main version** | `https://fabianofranca.github.io/mapping/` | It is the published `main`. **Stable** channel. It can be installed as an app (PWA). |
| **Preview of a branch** | `https://fabianofranca.github.io/mapping/preview/` | A branch published before the merge (published on its own with every PR opened or updated; there is only one preview, the one from the last PR updated; for another branch, the maintainer triggers it in Actions › Deploy › Run workflow). **Preview** channel, a "PREVIEW — data kept apart from the main version" banner at the top and a PREVIEW badge. Local projects are not mixed with those of the main version. |
| **Standalone `index.html`** | At `https://github.com/fabianofranca/mapping/actions/workflows/deploy.yml`, filter by branch `main` (**Branch** › `main`) and open the most recent run with ✓; at the end of the page, under **Artifacts**, `index-html` (or `index-html-preview`, in a preview run). Download, unzip and open the `index.html` with a double click (`file://`). | It works without internet and without a server. The home screen shows the notice "Opened as a file: projects "on this device" may not be kept by the browser. On a computer, prefer Open folder.": over `file://`, use **Open folder**. It does not install as an app. |

In any option:

- **Project in a folder** (the `mapping.json` and the images stay in a folder of yours, on disk) only exists in **desktop Chrome or Edge**. It is the mode the MCP server sees and the one you version with git.
- **Project on this device** (stored in the browser) works in the other browsers; to get the data out of there, export the zip.
- **Install as an app (PWA)** only from an `https:` address (main version or preview).
- **Minimum window of 900×720 px.** In a narrower or shorter window the app shows "Open in a larger window" in place of the screen; the project stays open and saving, and everything comes back when you widen or grow the window. Beware of DevTools docked on the side: it narrows the page. Dock it at the bottom or in a separate window.

## 2. Requirements

- A computer with an up-to-date **Chrome or Edge**, mouse and keyboard. There is no phone version: the app is desktop only.
- A **working folder** just for the tests (e.g. `~/mapping-tests/YYYY-MM-DD/`), where the projects, the zips and the report attachments live.
- A **text editor** to read and edit the `mapping.json` (any one; the JSON is readable). What the step asks for is the changed and saved file.
- **Test images:** the main script uses a screenshot of a sign-up screen (see R0). Any PNG or JPEG works for the others.
- **Extensions that touch the fields** (password managers such as LastPass, which inject a frame into text fields): disable them for the app's address. They get in the way of typing.
- **Specialization files** (`sdui.json` and `data-model.json`): in the repository, in `examples/specs/`; or through the app itself, in **Help** (F1), in the **Contents** list, the **Downloads** topic: "Download SDUI example (sdui.json)" and "Download Data model example (data-model.json)".
- **Example library** (Material 3 (Compose) package, R3.10 to R3.23, R9, R10, R12.12, R15 and A18): in the repository, the `libraries/material3-compose/` folder (206 files: the specialization, 50 components, 50 documents, 98 signature cards in `signatures/`, 4 in `fonts/` (the two fonts, the `LEIA-ME.txt` and the license) and 3 in `icons/`). The zip is `examples/material3-compose.zip` (below), with the content at the root; the zip with the root folder inside (R3.12) is built by the agent through the shell. Applying a **folder** only exists in Chrome/Edge.
- **Proposal example** `proposal-example.zip`: in the repository, in `examples/`.
- **Proposal example with new components** `proposal-components.zip` (R13): in the repository, in `examples/`; generated by `npm run build:proposal-components`.
- **Text-field suggestions example** `suggestions-kotlin.zip` (R14): in the repository, in `examples/`; generated by `npm run build:suggestions-kotlin`.
- **Material 3 (Compose) library** `material3-compose.zip` (R17): in the repository, in `examples/`; it is the `libraries/material3-compose/` package zipped (the content at the zip root), generated by `npm run build:material3-zip`.
- **Test image for remote images** (R15): in the repository, the file `public/test-images/photo.png` (the published app serves the same file at `…/test-images/photo.png`) and `scripts/image-server.mjs`; the type that shows the image is **Image** from the `libraries/material3-compose/` package. The Chrome computer needs **Node 20 or newer** for the local server of R15.1.
- **How to get the files in `examples/`:** clone the repository (`git clone https://github.com/fabianofranca/mapping`) or, on GitHub, open each file and use **Download raw file**. The "Download example…" items in Help go straight to the browser's downloads folder; move the files to the working folder.
- For **R3**, a test repository (section 6, step 2). Only for **R3.6, R3.21, R3.23 and R5** (MCP): **Node 20 or newer** (`node --version`), **Claude Code** installed and the `mapping-mcp.js` (section 6).
- **Folder permission: choose "Allow on every visit".** When you open a folder, Chrome and Edge ask for permission to see and edit the files. Whenever the **Allow on every visit** option appears (it may be at the first opening or only on a later visit), choose it: done once per folder, the browser stops asking.
- **Clean browser, or note what was already there.** Prefer a clean Chrome profile (or a new profile just for the tests). If you use a profile already used in another round, note in the report the projects the home screen already shows before you start. In this build, the first review discards once what earlier versions stored about the review: proposals already seen may come back as **New** and the review starts over (this is expected). R4.2 always starts from zero: the zip of R4.1 is a fresh copy. Do not delete projects from previous rounds without agreeing with the project maintainer.

## 3. Check which version is open

Every report carries the **build id**, in the format `abc1234 · YYYY-MM-DD` (the commit and the build date).

- With a project open: at the end of the **status bar** (the footer of the screen), after `schema v23` (the tooltip says "Format version: 23") and the channel (`stable` or `preview`).
- With no project open: in the **Settings** dialog (button on the side of the home screen), **About** section, at the end of the dialog and already open, with **Build**, **Channel** and **Format version**, and the **Copy** button.

The **channel** says which build the app came from, not where it was opened: **stable** (in Diagnostics, `channel: main`) for the main version, the app installed from it and the standalone `index.html` from the `index-html` artifact; **preview** (`channel: preview`) for `/preview/` and the `index-html-preview` artifact. That is why the report records both things: the channel and the way it was opened.

**The page may get stuck on an old version.** The app keeps a copy of itself (service worker) to open without internet; after a new publication, the browser may keep showing the previous one. Before testing a fix, check the build id against the expected commit. If it does not match:

1. If the **"New version available."** banner appears, click **Update**.
2. Otherwise, open the app in an **incognito window** or a **guest profile**. It starts clean, without touching the data of the normal window (but the incognito window erases everything on close: use a project in a **folder**, which stays on disk).
3. Last resort, in the normal window: DevTools (F12) › **Application** › **Service workers** › **Unregister** on the app's registration (the preview's has the scope ending in `/preview/`) and then **Storage** › **Clear site data**; reload. **Beware:** clearing the data **deletes the projects "on this device"** of the main version and of the preview (the origin is the same). Projects in a folder stay on disk (the app only asks again for the folder permission).

A publication made on another day may show "New version available" with no code change: the date is part of the build id.

## 4. How the app saves (read before checking the disk)

- **Autosave.** There is no Save button. The indicator is at the start of the status bar: **Saving…**, **Saved** or **Save failed** (with **Retry**). An ordinary edit saves about 250 ms later; actions in quick succession may go out in a single save.
- **Immediate save.** Adding or replacing images and applying, updating or removing specializations save right away. The app also saves when you switch tabs, minimize or leave.
- **Text fields save on confirm**: the name of a marking, image or annotation, and the key and value of a pair save with **Enter** or on leaving the field (Tab, click outside), not on every keystroke. Enter saves and the cursor **stays in the field**; in the Key of a pair, Enter moves to the Value. Leave the field with Tab or a click outside, and confirm before checking the disk.
- **"Leave page?"** If you close or reload the tab with something not yet saved, the browser asks whether you want to leave ("Leave site?" or "Leave page?"). **Choose to stay (Cancel or Stay) and wait for "Saved".** Leaving right away may lose the last edit.
- **Images are re-encoded.** When it enters the project, the image becomes WebP (lossless when the source is PNG), in `images/` with the `.webp` extension and the same dimensions: `cadastro.png` becomes `images/cadastro.webp`. If the WebP comes out larger than the original, the app keeps the original file with its extension (e.g. `.png`); it is not an error. The MCP follows the rule but encodes in Node: `cadastro.png` (11,487 bytes) gives 13,128 bytes of WebP in Chromium (the app keeps the `.png`) and 3,698 in Node (the MCP writes `.webp`).
- **Image name.** Added through the picker or dragged, the image keeps the file name. **Pasted** (`Ctrl+V`), it gets the name `img-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.webp`: where the step cites `cadastro.webp`, read the name the app gave.
- **Changes made from outside are only seen with the page visible.** Every ~3 s, and when focus returns to the window, the app checks whether the `mapping.json` changed outside it (R3.5, R6.3, R6.10). With the window covered, minimized or the screen locked, the check waits. Keep the window in view **and focused** during the round.
- **New proposals.** The **Proposals** window also checks the `proposals/` folder every ~3 s. If a proposal does not show up in ~3 s, use **Check the folder now** in the Proposals window.
- **System pickers only open with the window focused.** **Download** (the "Save as"), **Open folder** and **Open zip** open system dialogs that the browser only shows with the Chrome window focused. Without focus, the click opens nothing and the app shows no error; the same with another tab active in the window (e.g. the guide tab): close it, click the Chrome window and try again.
- **Hidden files.** The `.gitignore` starts with a dot: in the macOS Finder, show hidden files with `Cmd+Shift+.`; on Windows it shows up normally.
- **Checking the disk.** In a project in a folder, the `mapping.json` raises the `revision` field by 1 on every save. Wait for **Saved** before reading. The file is rewritten whole: if the read fails or comes back cut off, wait 1 s and read again.
- **Structure of the `mapping.json`** (what you need to check): `schemaVersion` (23); `revision`; `project` with `id` and `name`; `pages[]`; `containers[]` with `id`, `pageId`, `file` (`null` without a file), `width`, `height`, `placement` and `parentId`; `markings[]` with `id`, `name`, `containerId`, `pageId` (`null` inside a container), `parentId`, `locked`, `floating` and `rect` (integers, **in pixels of the original image**; with `containerId` `null`, the canvas marking, **in canvas units**, even negative). The `parentId` is computed by the app from the geometry, never chosen.
- **Layers and annotations in the file:** `layers[]` with `id`, `name`, `color` and `spec` (`null` in a free layer; in a specialization layer, `{ "specId": "sdui", "layerId": "componentes" }`, for example); `specializations[]` (the applied ones); `platformRepos` (R3); `annotations[]` with `markingId`, `layerId`, `name` and `entries` (free pairs) or `type` and `values` (typed). Full reference: [`docs/FORMAT.md`](FORMAT.md).
- **New project (folder, on this device or created by the MCP):** it is born with the notes library applied, so the `mapping.json` has two layers, the first (**Layer 1**, free) and **Notes** (`spec` `{ "specId": "notas", "layerId": "notas" }`), and `notas` in `specializations[]`. Where a step counts layers or specializations, add **Notes**.
- **References and numbers in the file.** A reference (e.g. the `dado` of an Input) appears as an object between `{ }`, not as text in quotes; a number appears without quotes (e.g. `500`).
- **Files of the project in a folder:** `mapping.json`, `images/`, `.gitignore` (with the line `backups/`), `specs/` (copies of the applied specializations; every new project is born with `specs/notas/`, the notes library), `proposals/` (proposals from agents), `comments/` (the threads, one `<id>.json` per thread, and `comments/resolved/` for the resolved ones; **the app and the MCP write there, never in the `mapping.json`**, and the thread does not enter undo) and `backups/` (copies of the `mapping.json` before a migration or a repair, `mapping.v<version>.<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.json`).

## 5. Interface map

The names in bold are the exact texts of the interface in English (en-US). Several controls are only icons: the name the guide uses is the **tooltip**, which appears with the mouse resting on the control. The explanations (field and type description, "Linked to", the marking and arrow lock) are an **ⓘ** icon (**About …** button) next to the label: the explanation appears in the tooltip on hover or on focus with Tab, Enter pins the tooltip and Esc closes it; there is no explanation text written below the field.

**Home screen.** **Get started**, **New project**, **Open folder**, **Open zip** and **Open library**; on the side, **Projects**, **Help**, **Interactive guide** (a separate page, opened in another tab), **Settings** (and **Install**, when it can be installed). The **Recent projects** list has the columns **Name**, **Source** (badge **Folder** or **On this device**) and **Last used**; each row has **Open** and, depending on the source, **Delete** or **Remove from list**.

**Main bar** (top of the editor), from left to right:

| Control | How it looks | Shortcut |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Project actions** (Export, Close project) | button with the project name and an arrow (accessible name: `<project>: project actions`) |  |
| **Navigate** / **Draw** | hand icon / pencil icon |  |
| **Add images** | icon with text |  |
| **New container** | icon with text, next to Add images (in narrow windows only the icon, with the tooltip on hover) |  |
| **Undo** / **Redo** | circular arrows backward / forward | `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z` |
| **Specializations** | icon with text |  |
| **Export** | icon with text | `Ctrl+E` |
| **Help** | question-mark icon | `F1` |
| **Settings** | gear | `Ctrl+,` |

**Layers window:** the **+** icon at the top is **New layer**; the eye icon is **Show all** (turns on the visibility of all layers); in each row, the color dot (tooltip "Color of layer …"), the **name**, which is a text field (click it to rename; Enter confirms), the visibility checkbox ("Show layer <name>"; any layer can be hidden, including the last visible one, and nothing is disabled) and the ⋮ **More actions for layer …**. At the bottom, the **Markings without annotations** list, with the options **Show all**, **Dim without annotations** and **Hide without annotations**.

**Canvas bar:** in the narrow bar the **…** opens the full path and, in review, the **⋯** holds what disappears. **View** (eye icon, `Alt+H`: view mode, the canvas for viewing only; it toggles, opens the **Show on canvas** panel and goes back to off when a project is opened), the **Show on canvas** button next to it (only enabled in the mode; reopens the panel), **Fit all** (`Shift+1`), **Fit selection** (icon of four corners with a square, `Shift+2`: zooms and centers the view on the selected items, without changing the selection or the project; disabled without a selection and in view mode, and with focus in a field `Shift+2` belongs to the field) and the zoom. In the mode, nothing is selected or edited, **Draw** is disabled and the status bar says "View mode: view only. Esc or Alt+H exits."; the panel chooses what the canvas shows (Containers, Images, Marking outlines, Marking names, Arrows and one box per layer with a drawing, with **Show all** and **Screens only** at the bottom) and the choice is kept per project, in this browser, without being saved to the `mapping.json`. The current zoom also appears in the status bar. The **canvas background** is the area around the images, outside them; if the image fills the whole view, zoom out (`Ctrl+-`) until the background shows. `Ctrl+=` and `Ctrl+-` zoom in and out about 25% per press and `Ctrl+0` goes back to the initial zoom; the wheel with Ctrl makes bigger jumps. 100% is not 1 image pixel per screen pixel.

**Tool windows** (they open and close from the icon strip on the edges or by the shortcut): **Tree** `Ctrl+Shift+1`, **Layers** `Ctrl+Shift+2` (or `Ctrl+L`), **Details** `Ctrl+Shift+3` and, in the bottom window, **List** `Ctrl+Shift+4`, **Incomplete** `Ctrl+Shift+5`, **Diagnostics** `Ctrl+Shift+6`, **Proposals** `Ctrl+Shift+7`, **Notices** `Ctrl+Shift+8` and **Comments** `Ctrl+Shift+0`; the **Conversation** window has no shortcut: it stacks under Details in the right column and opens with any conversation (a row of **Comments** or of the Details **Conversations** section, a pin, a citation chip, **New**, **Comment**) or from its button in the right strip; in a narrow bottom window (with the side windows open at 900×720) **Notices** and **Diagnostics** show only the icon, with the count and the tooltip; the **Catalog** window is on the left side, with `Ctrl+Shift+9`; it has the tabs **Components** (the catalog of the applied packages) and **Palette** (the list of types with Add; a new project already brings the **Note**). Opening or closing a window keeps the center and zoom of the view. Selecting an item in the **Tree** centers the selection and, if the marking does not fit well in the view, also changes the zoom: select first and zoom in afterwards. With focus in a text field, the shortcuts act on the field (`Ctrl+Z` undoes the text; `Ctrl+Shift+5` may type into it): click the canvas background first, or use the bar buttons.

**Incomplete in a narrow bottom window** (up to 470 px, for example at 900×720 with Tree, Layers and Details open): there is no **Layer** column; the layer (dot and name, with the full name in the tooltip) shows below the marking in the **Marking** cell. At 1280×720 the **Layer** column is back. The headers are never cut without an ellipsis.

**In the review of a proposal,** the **Proposals** window shows the review list, with the **Level** column: that is where the change badges are (Created, Removed, Moved, Changed, Image replaced, **Conflict**). The Tree, the Layers, List and Incomplete windows, the minimap, the selection path above the canvas and the status bar show the project of the open view (**Current** or **Proposed**), without badges. **Details** shows the item's normal panel (the usual fields, read-only), with a marker on each changed field: hover it or reach it with `Tab` to see the current value, the proposed one and the decision on that field; the decision on the whole item is in the header, right below the name. **Accept all** and **Reject all** are in the review bar (with a filter on, **Accept N shown**); in a window narrower than 1200 px, the two are in the **Bulk** menu.

**Other shortcuts:** `Alt+Shift+A` **Arrange** the selected container (R9); `Alt+L` locks or unlocks the selection; `Alt+H` turns view mode on or off (**View**); `Ctrl+C` copies the reference of the selected item; **Delete** or **Backspace** deletes the selection; **Esc** cancels a gesture, closes the menu, the dialog, the **Show on canvas** panel and, with focus inside them and outside a field, **Details**, **Comments** and **Catalog** (focus goes to the strip button; the selection stays) and, in view mode, leaves the mode. In a field with unsaved text, the first Esc goes back to the saved value; the second closes the dialog.

**On macOS:** in the shortcuts with `Ctrl`, the app also accepts `Cmd` (`Cmd+Z`, `Cmd+Shift+Z`, `Cmd+=`, `Cmd+C`, `Cmd+E`…); only `Ctrl+Y` (redo) has no `Cmd` version. For the windows, use `Ctrl+Shift+number`, because `Cmd+Shift+3`, `4` and `5` take a screenshot on macOS. `Alt` is the **Option** key. The Mac **delete** key deletes the selection (the app accepts Delete and Backspace). `F1` may require `fn+F1`. Browser shortcuts: reload is `Cmd+R` (F5 on Windows); close the tab, `Cmd+W` (`Ctrl+W`); and DevTools opens with `Cmd+Option+I` (F12).

**Add an image**, in three ways, with the same result:

1. **Add images** in the main bar (file picker);
2. **drag** the file from the file manager onto the canvas background, outside the image (dropping **onto an image** replaces that image, instead of adding);
3. **paste** (`Ctrl+V`) with the image on the clipboard and focus outside any text field (click the canvas background first, outside the image).

**Export › Download:** in Chrome and Edge it always opens the system "Save as". Choose the working folder and **Save** (if a file with the same name already exists, change the name or confirm the replacement). Once the file is saved, the Export dialog closes and, in a project on this device, the **Unexported changes** notice goes away. **Cancel** on the "Save as" exports nothing: the dialog and the notice stay. If the dialog also shows **Share**, ignore it: the steps use **Download**.

**Create a marking:** **Draw** mode and drag over the image. A marking drawn **inside** another becomes its child (who contains whom is decided by geometry, on release; in Details, **Belongs to** only shows the result). Dragging on the **canvas background**, outside the containers, creates a canvas marking (dashed border), which can wrap whole containers (R12). **Esc** cancels a gesture in progress. Dragging near the handles of the selected marking resizes it instead of creating another: before drawing a child, click the canvas background, outside the image, to clear the selection, or zoom in.

**Create an annotation:** select the marking. In **Details**, in the **Annotations** section, each layer has a **+** icon ("Add annotation to layer …"): use that icon on the layer the step asks for. In a free layer, the annotation has a name and pairs (**+ Pair**, **Key** and **Value** fields). In a specialization layer, the app asks for the type and shows its fields. Collapsed, the annotation shows a one-line summary (e.g. **Class · Contact**). In a table (e.g. `attributes`), the ⋮ at the end of each row opens its actions (tooltip "Actions for row …"). With an issue, **Annotations** in Details shows a box with ⚠ (on screen, a triangle) and the title "Incomplete: N issues".

**Script notation:** "**Age** › **Input** · `id` = `input_age`, `inputType` = `number`" means: select the marking **Age**, create on it an annotation of type **Input** (the **+** icon of the type's layer, here **Components**) and fill in the fields `id` and `inputType` with those values.

## 6. Install the MCP server (R3, R3.6 and R5)

The server lets an agent (Claude Code) read projects in a folder and **propose** changes; whoever writes the `mapping.json` is always the app. R3 uses only step 2 (the test repository); without the MCP, do only that, without copying the `mapping-mcp.js` or creating the `.mcp.json`. Summary of [`docs/MCP.md`](MCP.md):

1. Download the `mapping-mcp.js` and its `.sha256` from the latest `mcp-v…` Release of the repository (GitHub › Releases) and check the file: `sha256sum -c mapping-mcp.js.sha256` (on Windows, compare with `certutil -hashfile mapping-mcp.js SHA256`). Then `node mapping-mcp.js --version` must print the Release number, which is the version in `mcp/version.ts` on `main`.
   - **If the Release does not exist yet** for the `main` version: ask the project maintainer to create it ("Publishing a version" section of `docs/MCP.md`). If you cannot wait, build the file from the cloned repository, with Node 22: `npm ci && npm run build:mcp` (it comes out at `dist-mcp/mapping-mcp.js`), and write in the report "MCP built locally from commit `<sha>`".
   - **To test something not yet published**, use a pre-release from the same page: in a phase PR, `mcp-snapshot-pr<N>` (the PR build, which disappears when it closes); in the epic, `mcp-v<version>-rc.<n>` (it only exists after the merge of the PR with the `mcp-rc` label, the one of the last phase). `--version` prints the version with a suffix (`-snapshot.pr<N>+<sha>`, `-rc.<n>`).
2. Inside the working folder, create a test repository (`git init`), copy the file to `tools/mapping-mcp.js` and create the projects folder (e.g. `design/mapeamentos/`) and the `assets/` folder, with a copy of `cadastro.png` and `sdui.json`. The server only reads files inside the `--root` folders (the **roots**); outside them, Claude Code cannot add an image or apply a specialization (`outside-roots`).
3. At the root of that repository, create the `.mcp.json`:

   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "mapping": {
         "command": "node",
         "args": [
           "tools/mapping-mcp.js",
           "--root",
           "design/mapeamentos",
           "--root",
           "assets"
         ]
       }
     }
   }
   ```

4. Open Claude Code at the root of that repository and approve the `mapping` server. The tools appear as `mcp__mapping__…`. If they do not appear, see "Troubleshooting" in `docs/MCP.md`.
5. In the app, create or open the test projects **as a folder** inside `design/mapeamentos/`.

**Timing (cloud agent):** mark this section with `mark(apoioDir, 'secao6', 'start')` at the start and `mark(apoioDir, 'secao6', 'end')` at the end (or, from the shell, `APOIO=<folder>/apoio node scripts/testing/cloud.mjs mark secao6 start|end`), like the scripts.

**Repository with `"type": "module"` in `package.json`** (your real repository, not the test one, which starts empty): the `mapping-mcp.js` needs a `package.json` with `{"type":"commonjs"}` in the `tools/` folder. Details in `docs/MCP.md`.

Image limits: by `base64`, up to 16 MB per image; larger ones go by `file` (up to 64 MB and 40 megapixels). Above that the response is `image-too-large`.

**What Claude Code answers.** In the MCP steps, the expected result comes first as Claude Code describes the outcome, in prose. The technical detail comes in parentheses; to check it, ask Claude Code to "show the raw response of the tool".

## 7. How to report a problem

1. Open **Diagnostics**: the **Diagnostics** tab of the bottom window (`Ctrl+Shift+6`).
2. Click **Copy**. It works even with no errors logged. The text starts with a header, one piece of information per line, with the keys in English: `build`, `channel`, `schema`, `storage` (`folder` or `local`), `userAgent`, `window`, `language`, `theme`, the counts on a single line (e.g. `containers: 1, markings: 6, annotations: 11`), `pendingSave` and `errors`; then come the errors, the most recent first. It carries no project names, image names or paths.
3. With no project open, use the **Settings** dialog, **About** section (at the end), **Copy** button (build, channel and schema).
4. Gather: the copied text, the exact steps, the expected and the observed, a screenshot and, if it is a save problem, a copy of the `mapping.json` at that moment. Use the [report template](#10-templates) and open an issue at [github.com/fabianofranca/mapping/issues](https://github.com/fabianofranca/mapping/issues) or hand the report to whoever asked for the test. The cloud agent delivers the report as a comment on the sub-issue named in the round message. The issue opened for a defect carries the `bug` label, and the screenshot follows "Bugs and visual evidence" in `docs/PROCESS.md`.

**Severity** of each finding:

- **blocks**: data loss, a project that does not open, or a save that fails silently.
- **high**: prevents completing a flow, with no workaround.
- **medium**: there is a workaround, but whoever has not read this guide trips over it.
- **low**: cosmetic or text.

In the `bug` issue, the severity becomes a label: **blocks** and **high** → `severity: high`, **medium** → `severity: medium`, **low** → `severity: low`. Before opening the issue, check whether there is already an identical one or one that groups the defect ("Bugs and visual evidence" in `docs/PROCESS.md`).

**Browser console (optional).** If you use DevTools, keep the console visible during the test (F12, or `Cmd+Option+J` on Mac): any error in red is a finding. Without the console, the app's errors also appear in **Diagnostics** (item 1). Two console errors are known and do not count:

- `[open.repair] …` right after a **Repair and open**: it is the expected log of the repair (it also goes to Diagnostics);
- `[open.migration] …` when opening a migrated v10 or v12 project (R3.8b, R3.8d): it is the log of what the migration discarded, like `[open.repair]` (it also goes to Diagnostics);
- in the standalone `index.html` (`file://`), `ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` for `icons/icon.svg` on every load: the standalone file does not carry the `icons/` folder (a recorded pending item).

Also counted as a finding: noticeable slowness (more than a second to respond), cut-off or overlapping text, a horizontal scroll bar in a dialog or window (the table of a `table` field in Details scrolls in its own box on purpose: it only counts if the bar belongs to the panel), keyboard focus lost after closing a dialog and the tab crashing (record the Chrome version, at `chrome://version`).

## 8. Test scripts

**Conventions.**

- Each step has a code (e.g. **R2.3**), the **Action** and the **Expected**: **Screen** (what appears) and, when it saves, **Disk** (what stays in the `mapping.json` or in the folder). In the report, mark each code with ✅, ❌ or "not executed (reason)".
- Text in **bold** or in quotes is the exact text of the interface in English (en-US); the name of an icon is that of the tooltip (section 5).
- Text fields save with **Enter** (the cursor stays in the field) or on leaving the field; wait for **Saved** before reading the disk (section 4).
- How to create markings and annotations, how to add an image and the notation "**Marking** › **Type** · field = value" are in section 5; "draw" is always in **Draw** mode.
- _Italics at the end of the Expected_ mark a **known regression**: something that already broke in a previous round and is checked again, not the goal of the step.
- **[person]** marks the steps the cloud agent does not do alone (appendix A); whoever tests by hand can ignore the mark. The "or `action`" names the recipe that replaces the person in native dialogs (`select_folder`, `save_file`, `open_file`, `accept_permission_prompt`, `cancel_dialog`; each name is a recipe in appendix A, "Native dialogs in the cloud (Xvfb)") and the MCP client over stdio in the requests to Claude Code. In the main scripts no step is left without a substitute (a test checks).
- **Who changes the guide: marked passages.** `round-guide.mjs` generates the guide with only the requested scripts (also by step range, `R6.3-R6.7`). A passage of this introduction or of appendix A that only certain scripts use goes between `<!-- roteiros: R12 R22 -->` and `<!-- /roteiros -->`, on their own lines; it only enters the guide if one of them is requested. Without a mark, it goes in all of them (when in doubt, do not mark).
- **Rule for whoever changes the scripts (agents and people).** The main scripts (R0 to R43) are made for the cloud agent to run **alone**: every new or changed step needs a way for the cloud agent to do it (cloud recipe from appendix A, Playwright over CDP, shell or MCP client over stdio) and must say so in the Action.
- **A test that needs the owner.** If a test needs interaction from the owner (no cloud recipe does it) and **is not very relevant**, it goes to the **on-demand scripts (manual)** (end of this section), which the owner does by hand.
- **A test that needs the owner and is very relevant.** If it needs interaction from the owner and **is very relevant** (risk of data loss, integrity of the `mapping.json`, security), the agent **does not decide alone**: it warns the owner, in the conversation and in the PR description, so they decide together; until they decide, the step stays where it is, marked as **pending decision**.

**Full or directed round.** The **full round** runs all the scripts, in the order of "Start here"; it is the gate before use with people. In the cloud it can run in blocks at the same time, each with its report (the split is in `docs/TESTING-NUVEM.md`, "Full round in blocks"). The **directed round** checks a target: the findings of a previous report (the report is a comment on an issue), a list of scripts or the phases of a stage. In all of them, the whole R0 first, then only the steps tied to the target. The directed round's report uses the same template (section 10), with the **Originating finding** column and the **Regressions outside the target** section.

### R0 — Setup and smoke test

Prepare the screenshot of the sign-up screen, if you do not have one yet: save the HTML below as `cadastro.html` in the working folder (in Notepad, under **Save as type**, choose "All files", otherwise the file comes out as `cadastro.html.txt`; in macOS TextEdit, first use **Format** › **Make Plain Text**) and open it in Chrome. With the system capture tool (on Windows, `Win+Shift+S`; on macOS, `Cmd+Shift+4` and drag), capture the area with the title, the three fields and the button, and save it as `cadastro.png` in the working folder. At 100% scale that area is about 484 px wide; at 125% or on a Retina Mac the capture comes out larger (e.g. ~605 px or ~968 px), which is fine: what matters is the content.

**Checking the size of a PNG:** on Windows, right-click › Properties › Details; on macOS, Get Info › More Info. Alternative: F12, `Ctrl+Shift+P`, "Capture full size screenshot" and Enter (484 × ~450 px, in the downloads folder).

```html
<!doctype html>
<meta charset="utf-8" />
<body style="font: 20px sans-serif; width: 420px; margin: 0; padding: 32px">
  <h1>Create your account</h1>
  <form>
    <p>Name<br /><input style="width: 340px; font: inherit" /></p>
    <p>Age<br /><input style="width: 340px; font: inherit" /></p>
    <p>Email<br /><input style="width: 340px; font: inherit" /></p>
    <p><button style="font: inherit; padding: 12px 32px">Register</button></p>
  </form>
</body>
```

### R1 — Main script, project in a folder

Use an empty folder `principal` and the `cadastro.png`. After each step that saves, wait for **Saved** and check the disk as the step says. These save nothing (the `revision` stays the same): R1.5, R1.13, R1.17, R1.19, R1.19a, R1.20, R1.20a, R1.20d, R1.21, R1.21a, R1.21b (layer visibility, zoom and filters belong to the screen, not to the project), R1.21d and R1.22. R1.20b and R1.20c do save: R1.20b prepares the Note and the arrow (two saves, `revision` +1 on each) and R1.20c deletes them (two more), so that R1.21 onward finds the project as it was. In all the others, always: `revision` greater than in the previous step, `rect` in pixels of the original image and no `file` that does not exist in `images/`.

**Preparing R1.21a (6) and (7).** The `principal` has no proposal: before (6), through the stdio client (`--root` on the working folder), send a `propose_changes` with two new layers (the **Proposals** window only shows what the client sent). For (7): choose, with `select_folder` **[person]**, a copy of `libraries/material3-compose/` in the working folder.

**Preparing R1.20b and R1.20c (through Playwright/CDP, once, right before R1.20b).** The `principal` has no arrow or layer with drawings. ### R3 — Specialization code

**Prerequisite:** section 6 (the test repository with `git init`, `tools/mapping-mcp.js`, the `design/mapeamentos/` and `assets/` folders and the `.mcp.json`). Without the MCP, step 2 of it is enough: R3.1 to R3.5 do not use the server, only R3.6, R3.21 and R3.23 do. Use the R1 `principal` project (with SDUI and the Data model applied); if the round does not include R1, build it beforehand through the MCP (`create_project` and `propose_changes`, reviewed in the app): the two specializations, the **Signup** container (`cadastro.png`) and the **Form**, **Name**, **Age**, **Email** and **Register** markings. Move the folder, with the project closed, to `design/mapeamentos/principal` inside that repository. Once moved, **Open** on the `principal` row of the recents leads to the **Folder unavailable** notice: use **Locate folder…**, choose the folder in the new place **[person]** and allow editing **[person]** (both, or `select_folder`); from then on the row opens the new place.

**Preparing R3.8, R3.8b, R3.8c, R3.8d, R3.8e and R3.9** (only for them; there is no ready-made v8 or v10 project, because the app only saves v14). With a text editor or the shell:

1. Copy `sdui.json` to `sdui-antigo.json` and, in the `screen` type (in `layers[].annotationTypes[]`, the one with `"id": "screen"`), add at the end of the `fields` list the field `{ "key": "implementacao", "label": "implementation", "type": "codeRef" }`: that is how old specializations declared the removed field.
2. In the app, create the `migracao` folder (**Open folder** on a new folder, **[person]** or `select_folder`), add `cadastro.png`, draw a marking, apply the **normal** `sdui.json` and create a **Screen** on it with `name` = `Signup` and `route` = `/signup`. Wait for **Saved** and close the project.
3. Outside the app: in `migracao/mapping.json`, change `"schemaVersion": 23` to `8`, the key `"containers"` to `"images"` and, in each marking, `"containerId"` to `"imageId"` (this is the real v8 format; without this change the app refuses the file) and add to the Screen's `values` `"implementacao": [ { "_id": "c1", "platform": "android", "path": "app/src/main/java/com/app/SignupScreen.kt", "symbol": "SignupScreen", "line": null } ]`; replace `migracao/specs/sdui.json` with `sdui-antigo.json`. Keep a copy of that `mapping.json` (it is the "v8 project").
4. For R3.8b (v10 project with `urlTemplate`), create the `migracao10` folder the same way: `cadastro.png`, one marking, the **normal** `sdui.json` and a `Signup` **Screen** at `/signup`. Wait for **Saved** and close the project.
5. Outside the app, in `migracao10/mapping.json`, change `"schemaVersion": 23` to `10`, `"containers"` to `"images"` and `"containerId"` to `"imageId"` (as in step 3) and leave `platformRepos` like this: `{ "android": { "urlTemplate": "https://github.com/org/app/blob/main/{path}", "localPath": "../app" }, "ios": { "urlTemplate": "https://github.com/org/app-ios/blob/main/{path}", "localPath": null } }`. Keep a copy of that `mapping.json` (it is the "v10 project"); the SDUI copy in `specs/` stays as it is.
6. For R3.8c (v11 project, the one before the container), create the `migracao11` folder: `cadastro.png` and one marking, then **Saved** and close the project. Outside the app, through the shell (or an editor), in `migracao11/mapping.json` change `"schemaVersion": 23` to `11`, the key `"containers"` to `"images"` and, in each marking, `"containerId"` to `"imageId"`. Keep a copy of that `mapping.json` (it is the "v11 project").
7. For R3.8d (v12 project with inheritance), create the `migracao12` folder: `cadastro.png` and two markings, one **parent** and, inside it, one **child**; on the parent, create a **free** annotation (free layer, pair `style` = `primary`). **Saved** and close the project. Through the shell (or an editor), in `migracao12/mapping.json`: `"schemaVersion": 23` becomes `12`; the parent's annotation gets `"inherit": true` (others, if any, `false`); remove `"floating"` from each marking and `"parentId"` from each container (v12 does not have them). Keep a copy (the "v12 project").
8. For R3.8e (v13 project, the one before roles in the link), you do not need to open the app: through the shell, the `migracao13` folder with a small schema 13 `mapping.json` (a container with no image, the **Box** marking and two free annotations in different layers: **Owner** and, linked to it, **Child**):

   ```bash
   if [ -e migracao13 ]; then echo 'migracao13 already exists: the setup already ran; do not run it again'; else
   mkdir -p migracao13 && cat > migracao13/mapping.json <<'EOF'
   {"schemaVersion":13,"revision":0,"app":"mapping","coordinateSystem":"image-pixels-exif-oriented","project":{"name":"Migracao13","createdAt":"2026-11-05T12:00:00.000Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-05T12:00:00.000Z"},"specializations":[],"platformRepos":{},"layers":[{"id":"L1","name":"Layer 1","color":"#E53935","spec":null},{"id":"L2","name":"Layer 2","color":"#1E88E5","spec":null}],"containers":[{"id":"C1","name":"Screen","file":null,"width":400,"height":300,"placement":{"x":0,"y":0,"scale":1},"parentId":null,"markingColor":null,"locked":false,"source":null,"background":"#FFFFFF"}],"markings":[{"id":"M1","containerId":"C1","parentId":null,"name":"Box","rect":{"x":20,"y":20,"width":200,"height":100},"needsReview":false,"locked":false,"floating":false,"source":null}],"arrows":[],"annotations":[{"id":"A1","markingId":"M1","layerId":"L1","name":"Owner","parentAnnotationId":null,"type":null,"values":null,"entries":[{"id":"E1","key":"style","value":"primary"}]},{"id":"A2","markingId":"M1","layerId":"L2","name":"Child","parentAnnotationId":"A1","type":null,"values":null,"entries":[{"id":"E2","key":"note","value":"x"}]}]}
   EOF
   cp migracao13/mapping.json migracao13-original.json   # the "v13 project"
   fi
   ```

**Preparing R3.14 to R3.17** (new versions of Material 3 (Compose), with migration). Save the script below as `evolve.py`, outside the app's repository, and, with the shell at its root and `python3` available, generate the four chained copies, `mat-v19` to `mat-v22` (the number is the specialization version of each copy) (each one starts from the previous one, and the first from the repository package, which is already at version 18; the repository package does not change):

```python
import json, shutil, sys
src, dst, step = sys.argv[1:4]  # current folder, new folder, v5 | n1 | n2 | n3 | n4 (n<k> adds k to the version of the source folder's package)
shutil.copytree(src, dst)
p = dst + '/material3-compose.spec.json'
s = json.load(open(p))
cur = s['version']  # the version of the source folder: every copy of the chain is relative to it
types = [t for l in s['layers'] for t in l['annotationTypes']]
fab = next(t for t in types if t['id'] == 'fab')
if step == 'v5':  # the previous package: the slider with value in tenths (enum), without migrations
    s['version'] = 5
    s.pop('migrations', None)
    tenths = [str(i / 10).rstrip('0').rstrip('.') or '0' for i in range(11)]
    slider = next(t for t in types if t['id'] == 'slider')
    for f in slider['fields']:
        if f['key'] in ('value', 'valueStart', 'valueEnd'):
            f['type'], f['options'], f['default'] = 'enum', tenths, str(f['default'])
    slider['examples'] = [e for e in slider.get('examples', []) if all(str(e['values'][k]) in tenths for k in ('value', 'valueStart', 'valueEnd') if k in e['values'])]
    for e in slider['examples']:
        e['values'] = {k: (str(v) if k in ('value', 'valueStart', 'valueEnd') else v) for k, v in e['values'].items()}
elif step == 'n1':  # additive: new optional field
    s['version'] = cur + 1
    s.pop('migrations', None)
    fab['fields'].append({'key': 'note', 'label': 'Note', 'type': 'string'})
elif step == 'n2':  # containerColor -> tone
    s['version'] = cur + 1
    for f in fab['fields']:
        if f['key'] == 'containerColor': f['key'], f['label'] = 'tone', 'Tone'
    code = fab['code']['compose']
    for k in ('params', 'values'):
        code[k] = {'tone' if a == 'containerColor' else a: b for a, b in code[k].items()}
    for e in fab.get('examples', []):
        if 'containerColor' in e['values']: e['values']['tone'] = e['values'].pop('containerColor')
    c = dst + '/components/fab.json'
    t = open(c).read().replace('"$switch": "containerColor"', '"$switch": "tone"').replace('"containerColor": "primaryContainer"', '"tone": "primaryContainer"')
    open(c, 'w').write(t)
    s['migrations'] = [{'from': cur, 'to': cur + 1, 'steps': [{'op': 'rename-field', 'type': 'fab', 'from': 'containerColor', 'to': 'tone'}]}]
elif step == 'n3':  # removes the note field
    s['version'] = cur + 1
    fab['fields'] = [f for f in fab['fields'] if f['key'] != 'note']
    s['migrations'].append({'from': cur, 'to': cur + 1, 'steps': [{'op': 'remove-field', 'type': 'fab', 'field': 'note'}]})
elif step == 'n4':  # removes a type WITHOUT migration
    s['version'] = cur + 1
    for l in s['layers']:
        l['annotationTypes'] = [t for t in l['annotationTypes'] if t['id'] != 'badge']
json.dump(s, open(p, 'w'), ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
```

```bash
M=libraries/material3-compose
N=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('$M/material3-compose.spec.json'))['version'])")   # the package's version today: the copies are N+1 to N+4
python3 evolve.py $M mat-v5 v5   # the previous package (the slider in tenths), only for R3.14
python3 evolve.py $M mat-v$((N+1)) n1 && python3 evolve.py mat-v$((N+1)) mat-v$((N+2)) n2 \
  && python3 evolve.py mat-v$((N+2)) mat-v$((N+3)) n3 && python3 evolve.py mat-v$((N+3)) mat-v$((N+4)) n4
```

The `mat-v5` copy (outside the chain) is the previous package: version 5, without `migrations` and with the slider's `value`, `valueStart` and `valueEnd` as `enum` in tenths. What each copy in the chain changes in the `fab` type (FAB): **n1** (v19), the optional `note` field (additive, without `migrations`); **n2** (v20), `containerColor` ("Button color") renamed to `tone`, with `rename-field` in `migrations` (the field label becomes "Tone" and the component and the examples follow); **n3** (v21), the `note` field removed, with `remove-field`; **n4** (v22), the `badge` type (Badge) removed **without** `migrations` (the files `components/badge.json`, `docs/badge.md`, `signatures/badge.compose.json` and `signatures/badge.large.compose.json` stay in the folder, orphaned).

All the scripts start from **new projects**: `sdui.json` changed (it gained `path` and lost the `implementacao` field) without bumping the version, and a project created before does not receive the new file through **Update version…**. Use MCP 0.4.0 (section 6).

### R4 — Proposals without an agent (with the `proposal-example.zip`)

The zip brings the **Store** project (**Checkout** and **Cart** images, the **Pay button** marking locked) and the proposal **"Checkout from Figma"**: it creates the Events layer and the **Confirmation** image (with the Success message marking), replaces the Cart's image, renames **Header**, moves the Pay button, creates **Coupon field** (with an Input annotation), removes **Promo banner** and changes annotations. "Review list" is the list in the Proposals window during the review, with the **Level** column (section 5).

**Preparing R4.19.** The interface does not reach the step's state on its own (accepting the marking accepts the image along with it), so build it through the shell in two disposable copies of the unzipped `proposal-example.zip`, `loja-bloq` and `loja-bloq1`. In each one's `proposal.json`, put in `decisions` only `c7` = `{ "state": "accepted", "at": "2026-11-09T03:10:00.000Z" }` (the **Success message** marking, which depends on the **Confirmation** image, `c3`). Only in `loja-bloq`, add at the end of `changes` a second pending change on the image: `{ "id": "c12", "entity": "image", "entityId": "I3", "imageId": "I3", "markingId": null, "kind": "update", "field": "name", "from": "Confirmation", "to": "Confirmation v2" }`.

R7.2 procedure:

1. With the `principal` closed, copy the `principal` folder to `principal-reparo`, next to it, and delete the `backups/` folder from the **copy** (appendix B).
2. In the copy's `mapping.json`, change `project.name` to `principal-reparo` and save (without this, the copy opens with the same name, `principal`).
3. Open the copy with **Open folder** (**[person]** or `select_folder`: it is the first time for that folder; permission as in R0.2) and check `principal-reparo` on the project button, in the main bar.
4. Select **Form** and add to **User** the pair `extra` = `x` (Enter); wait for **Saved** and close the project.
5. In the copy's `mapping.json`, copy the `id` of the User's first pair (`fullname`) to the `extra` pair and save.
6. Open the copy from the home screen (`principal-reparo` row, **Open**) and use **Repair and open**.
7. Open Diagnostics, click **Copy** and paste into a text file.
8. Make any edit and wait for **Saved**.

### R5 — Proposals with an agent

It sits near the end because it needs you in Claude Code. It needs the MCP (section 6) and a folder project inside `design/mapeamentos/`. Before each request to Claude Code, note the `mapping.json` `revision`; afterwards, check that it did not change: Claude Code never changes a `mapping.json` that already exists; only the app does, when applying. The only exception is the `create_project` of R5.2, which creates the initial `mapping.json` of a new project.

Prepare a second screenshot, `login.png` (any login screen; it can be made like R0's `cadastro.png`, from an HTML with a title, email, password and a Sign in button), and put `login.png` in `assets/`, next to `cadastro.png` and `sdui.json` (section 6, step 2). In the requests to Claude Code, the files in `assets/` go by name, relative to that root: `sdui.json`, `cadastro.png` and `login.png`, and not `assets/sdui.json` (the server does not find the file: `path-not-found`).

| Step | Action | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R5.1 | In the app, open the `principal` (from the recents), select the **Name** marking and press `Ctrl+C`. **[person]** (or the stdio client: use the copied reference as the `resolve` argument) In Claude Code, ask to **list the projects**, paste the reference and ask to **describe it**; then ask for its **crop**. | **Screen:** the copied text is only the URL, `mapping://principal/m/<code>`, with nothing after the code (not even the readable path in parentheses). ### R9 — Containers with components

**What it covers:** the Library stage in the app (and the Container one): the **New container** dialog, the **Catalog** window (**Palette** tab, Esc), Material 3 components drawn on the canvas, the **Row** slot with chips and **Arrange**, the **Order**, live editing, the minimum size, the option about photos, the container's density (the suggestion from the preset size, Apply and the 3x drawing), the anchor between markings (the **Anchor** section, **Snap to anchor**, dragging the anchor and the link line), **Add** inside a component with named slots (the slot that takes the type, the note on the default-content fields and the pending item in the **Details**, with the `tests/fixtures/slots/` library), Diagnostics and a second container created by a proposal (`add_container`). **Rule to check at the end:** the `mapping.json` has nothing of the drawing.

**Setup.** New folder `telas` (folder project, **Open folder** **[person]** (or `select_folder`) as in R1; in Firefox or without a folder, a project on this device works up to R9.12). The package brings the **Roboto** font files (Regular and Medium): the texts come out in Roboto in the app **and** in the MCP's measurements and PNGs.

### R10 — Catalog

**What it covers:** the library's catalog page (B5): the Catalog opened from the home screen, **without a project** (package folder or zip), with the validation, the list by layer with search, each component's page and the live playground; and the **Catalog** window inside the project (**Components** and **Palette** tabs). **Rule to check at the end:** opening a library from the home screen saves nothing, neither in the package folder nor in the recent projects.

**Setup.** The package is `libraries/material3-compose/` (folder, or the `examples/material3-compose.zip` from section 2); R10.10 and R10.11 use the `examples/libraries/sdui-backend/` folder, the executable origin (the lean package, without fonts). **What it covers:** the interactive guide (the `guide/` page, published next to the `index.html`; the old `guia/` address only redirects) and the example project, the repository's `examples/full-example.zip`, opened through **Open zip** (the app does not embed it). **Rule to check at the end:** opening the example saves only what **Open zip** saves (a copy **On this device**), nothing in a folder.

### R12 — Canvas marking and containment by geometry

**What it covers:** the Spatial markings stages (ME1 to ME4): the canvas marking, containment by geometry saved in the `mapping.json`, dragging a container, **Wrap** and selecting several items (R12.8 to R12.13a), the order among siblings, notes, dragging from the Palette, arrows and tables beside the screen (R12.17 to R12.22). **Rule to check at the end:** the `parentId` is never chosen by anyone; it only changes when the geometry changes.

**Setup.** New folder `espaco` (**Open folder** **[person]** (or `select_folder`) as in R1; the script reads the disk, so a project on this device does not work). No image. Create three containers with **New container** › **Preset size** › **Custom**, each with **Width** `200`, **Height** `150`, **Background color** `#FFFFFF` and the names `A`, `B` and `C` (in that order). The three are born in a column near the view's center: in **Navigate** mode, select `B` with a click (without a selection the drag only moves the view) and drag it in two moves, first to the right until it passes `A` and then up to its height (a container stops when it touches another, so a diagonal drag touches `A` and stops). Do the same with `C`, to the right of `B`, leaving a gap of about 150 canvas px between `B` and `C`, and click **Fit all**. To read the disk with the project open, after **Saved**, run in the `espaco` folder: `python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('mapping.json'));print([(c['name'],c['id'],c['parentId'],c['placement']) for c in d['containers']]);print([(m['name'],m['id'],m['containerId'],m['parentId'],m['floating'],m['rect']) for m in d['markings']])"` (in PowerShell, `Get-Content mapping.json | ConvertFrom-Json`). Call this reading **read the disk**. **Stroke box (R12.10f).** With the arrow selected the `data-selection-box` is `null`: read the box from the crop, with `convert arrow.png -fuzz 6% -fill white +opaque '#4d8dff' -format '%@' info:` (`WxH+X+Y`; `#4d8dff` is the `--cv-arrow-select`, the same in both themes). Its center (`X + W/2`, `Y + H/2`) stays within 3 px of the `.canvas-host` center.

#### R12.23 to R12.28 — The MCP reads the space and the arrows

**What it covers:** ME5 (the MCP at the version of `mcp/version.ts`): `get_marking` of a canvas marking (`space`, `floating`, `members`, `arrows`); `create_marking` without `container` and `update_marking` with `container`; `create_arrow` and the annotation on the arrow; `get_marking_image` refusing the canvas marking and the arrow; and `create_project` with and without `notes`. **Rule to check at the end:** the agent **reads** `parent` and `members`, never computes containment, and `parent` in `create_marking`/`update_marking` comes as `ignored-argument`.

**Setup.** Steps R12.23 to R12.26 use the `setas` folder from R12.17 to R12.22 (already in `design/mapeamentos/setas`, with the `analytics` library applied in R12.19 and the table created by R12.20), open in the app through the `setas` row with the **Folder** badge (`state()` shows `Origem: Pasta`); R12.27 creates new folders. Everything through the stdio MCP client (section 6), `WS` with `design/mapeamentos` as the root; `create_project` takes `root` `design/mapeamentos` (without it, the error is `root-required`). Without the MCP, mark "not run (no MCP)".

Then `list_markings` with `canvas: true` and `container` `Home` together. | `get_project`: `counts` with `canvasMarkings` and `floatingMarkings` greater than 0 and `arrows` with the number of arrows from **read the arrows**; each container brings `parent` (`null`). `list_markings`: only markings with `space` `"canvas"`; the table has `floating` `true` and `container` `"Canvas"` (the space's name as text, without `path`). #### R12.34 to R12.40 — Anchor between markings through the MCP

**What it covers:** the anchor in the model and in the MCP (R3 of the Direction and anchor stage, schema v20, MCP at the version of `mcp/version.ts`): `create_marking` with `anchor` and **without `rect`** (the piece is born at the measured size, snapped), the `snap_to_anchor` op (a batch one: there is no tool of its own) alone and in the batch, the proposal with an anchor at `formatVersion` 9, `get_marking` and `get_code_hints` with the anchor, moving the anchor (takes the anchored ones) and resizing (does not), and the `anchor-*`, `not-anchored` and `locked` errors. The requests are MCP ones; the app only opens the folder and accepts the proposals. The cloud does all the steps alone.

**Setup.** Section 6 ready (the test repository and the `mapping-mcp.js`); the MCP requests are made through the stdio client (appendix A: `WS=<workspace> node scripts/testing/mcp-stdio-client.mjs calls.json`; arguments from `[{"list":true}]`). `ROOT` is the server's projects root (`design/mapeamentos` in section 6) and `REPO`, the Mapping clone. The tooltip is that of the `material3-compose` library, which declares `anchor` at the root (`top`, `center`, 4) and draws the arrow when the marking has an anchor: R12.35's request gives the side, the alignment and the offset (8), overriding the root's defaults. R12.34 creates the `ancora` folder and R12.35 accepts it; the others depend on it.

| Step | Action | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R12.34 | **The folder and the target.** Through the shell, `cp -r REPO/libraries/material3-compose ROOT/m3-r12`. Through the stdio client, `create_project` with `path` `ancora`, `name` `Anchor` and `root` `design/mapeamentos`; then `propose_changes` on that project (title "Target") with `apply_specialization` (`file` `m3-r12/material3-compose.spec.json`), `add_container` (`name` `Screen`, `width` 400, `height` 300, `background` `#FFFFFF`) and, in it, `create_marking` with `name` `Target` and `rect` `{ x: 150, y: 140, width: 100, height: 40 }`. In the app, **Open folder** `ancora` (**[person]** or `select_folder`), **Proposals** (`Ctrl+Shift+7`) › **Review**, **Accept all changes**, **Apply accepted**; wait for **Saved**. | **Client:** project created and valid proposal, 1 container and 1 marking created. **Disk:** `schemaVersion` 23; the `material3-compose` specialization applied; the `Screen` container (400 × 300, `#FFFFFF`) and the `Target` marking with `rect` `{"x":150,"y":140,"width":100,"height":40}`, `parentId` `null` and **no `anchor` key** (saved only with an anchor: `grep -c '"anchor"' ancora/mapping.json` gives `0`). |
| R12.35 | **`create_marking` with `anchor` and without `rect`.** Through the stdio client, `list_markings` and `get_marking` of the `Target` (its `ref`); then `propose_changes` (title "Tip") with `create_marking` in the `Screen` container (`name` `Tip`, `annotation` `{ "type": "material3-compose/tooltip" }` without `values`, **without `rect`**, `anchor` `{ "to": "<the Target's ref>", "side": "top", "align": "center", "offset": { "main": 8, "cross": 0 } }`, `as` `$tip`). In the app, **Review**, **Accept all changes**, **Apply accepted**; wait for **Saved** and **read the disk**. | **Disk:** the `Target` with `rect` `{"x":210,"y":160,"width":140,"height":40}`; the `Tip` with R12.35's `x` and `y` **plus 60 and plus 20** (same `width` and `height`: the move took it, the resize did not); the `Tip`'s `anchor` unchanged; `parentId` `null` on both. **Screen:** the `Tip` is no longer centered on the `Target` (it was only moved). |

#### R12.57 to R12.60 — A component keeps its units when it changes space

**What it covers:** a marking that draws a component (the Text of the notes library) keeps its size in component units when the geometry moves it between the canvas and a container of another density, a plain marking keeps its size on screen, and a set that moves together scales as a whole. **Rule to check at the end:** the density counts for a component and not for a plain marking; the scale counts for both.

**Setup.** New folder `units` (**Open folder** **[person]** (or `select_folder`) as in R1; no image; the notes library is applied at version 5). It depends on no other script. **New container** › **Custom**, `1000` × `600`, background `#FFFFFF`, **Density** `2x`, name `Screen` (its scale is 1000 ÷ 1000 = 1), and **Fit all**. To read the disk, after **Saved**, run in the `units` folder: `python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('mapping.json'));n={c['id']:c['name'] for c in d['containers']};print([(c['name'],c['placement'],c.get('density')) for c in d['containers']]);print([(m['name'],n.get(m['containerId']),m['floating'],m['rect'],m['parentId']) for m in d['markings']])"`. Call this reading **read the units**.

| Step | Action | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R12.57 | **The text enters a 2x container.** On empty canvas, **Palette** › **Text** › **Add**; set **Text** to `Label` and **Arrange**. **Read the units** and note the canvas `width` × `height` (`w0` × `h0`). Drag the text (Playwright `page.mouse`) until it falls entirely inside `Screen`, with its top-left about 40 canvas units inside `Screen`'s top-left. Wait for **Saved** and **read the units**. | **Screen:** on release the text is under `Screen` in the Tree and is drawn twice as big, with the box still fitting the text; Details shows no "Incomplete" and the text is not a dash. **Disk:** `containerId` = `Screen`, `rect` `2·w0` × `2·h0` (±1). |
| R12.58 | **Back to the canvas.** Drag the text out of `Screen` onto empty canvas. Wait for **Saved** and **read the units**. | **Screen:** the text is drawn at the size of R12.57 before the drop, with no "Incomplete". **Disk:** `containerId` `null`, `rect` `w0` × `h0` (±1). |
| R12.59 | **A plain marking keeps its size on screen.** In **Draw** mode, on the canvas background, draw a marking of about 100 × 50 and name it `Box`. **Read the units**, then drag `Box` entirely inside `Screen`. Wait for **Saved** and **read the units**. | **Screen:** `Box` has the same size on screen before and after. **Disk:** `containerId` = `Screen`, and `width` and `height` equal to the canvas ones (±1), because the scale is 1 and the density does not count for a plain marking. |

With `Area` selected, **Palette** › **Text** › **Add** (it is born inside `Area`). **Read the units**, then drag `Area` (it carries its descendants) out of `Screen` onto empty canvas. Wait for **Saved** and **read the units**. | **Screen:** `Area` and its text are both drawn at half the size on screen, and the text is still under `Area` in the Tree. **Disk:** `Area` and the text have `containerId` `null`; their `width` and `height` are half of those in `Screen` (±1), and the text's `parentId` is `Area`'s `id`. |

### R14 — Text-field suggestions and mapped targets

**What it covers:** the Text-field suggestions stage (SG1 and SG2): a text field or column whose specialization declares `suggestions` becomes a combobox, with a list of suggestions that **does not restrict** the value; with `linkedRef`, the list gains, before the fixed ones, the mapped declarations that the sibling `ref` accepts, and choosing one saves the text and the `ref` together. The Kotlin library (version 2, `formatVersion` 8) declares the fixed list of 24 types in Properties › Type and in Functions › Return type, and `linkedRef` (for **Mapped type**) in Properties › Type and Supertypes › Type; Functions › Return type has no `ref` beside it and only brings the fixed list. Steps R14.2 to R14.13 check the fixed list (which, in **User**, comes after the mapped target **Address**); R14.14 to R14.19, the mapped target.

**Setup.** The file is `suggestions-kotlin.zip` (in the repository, in `examples/`; section 2). It brings the **Kotlin Suggestions** project: a plain image and two data classes from the Kotlin library, **User** (Properties `id: Long`, `name: String`, `email: String?`, `address: Address` and `active` with the **Type** empty) and **Address** (`street: String`, `city: String`). In the **Tree** the two markings show as **Data class** (the first is **User**'s, the second **Address**'s); `User` and `Address` are the annotation's **Name** field, visible in **Details**. Where a step says to select **User** or **Address** in the **Tree**, it is the first or the second **Data class**. The fixed list (in this order; in Properties › Type it comes after the mapped targets): `String`, `Int`, `Long`, `Boolean`, `Double`, `Float`, `Short`, `Byte`, `Char`, `UInt`, `ULong`, `UShort`, `UByte`, `Any`, `Unit`, `Nothing`, `List`, `MutableList`, `Set`, `MutableSet`, `Map`, `MutableMap`, `Array`, `Pair`.

The agent checks the list through the DOM (the page's JavaScript, through Playwright): the field being edited has `role="combobox"` and `aria-expanded` (`true` with the list open, `false` closed); the list is an element `role="listbox"` with one `role="option"` per suggestion; the active option has `aria-selected="true"` and the others `aria-selected="false"`. Use the **Type** column of **User**'s `active` row (Details, `Ctrl+Shift+3`) for the steps that type; it (and its **Mapped type**) starts empty and goes back to empty when the step says to undo. In **User** the only mapped target is **Address** (the annotation itself is never its own target; **User** is a target in **Address**'s list); in the list, the mapped target is an option like the others, with its type's name (**Data class**) as secondary text inside the same `role="option"`. **Mapped type** is the `ref` column beside **Type**: empty, it shows the empty text; filled, it shows the target's label as the `ref` picker shows it: the declaration's name and its field, for example `Address.name` (tooltip "→ Address.name (Kotlin)"). The undo state is read through the bar's **Undo** button (enabled or disabled) and through the cell's text after `Ctrl+Z`. **`Ctrl+Z` with the focus inside the field is the browser's text undo**, which does not go through the app: before each `Ctrl+Z` in the steps, take the focus out of the field (for example, click the **Details** title). The list opens when typing a word with a match, with `ArrowDown`, with `Ctrl+Space` or with a click on an already empty field; **clearing the text does not open it**. Steps R14.10 and R14.11 add rows and, at the end, undo everything, so that **Undo** is disabled again and the following steps can measure it.

The read-only field (proposal review) does not show a list; this is covered by the component test `tests/components/Suggestions.test.tsx`, because the zip does not bring an open proposal.

### R15 — Remote images

**What it covers:** the Remote images stage (RI1 to RI3): the **Image** component of the `material3-compose` library shows a photo whose URL is the value of a field (`url`). Each step checks a security gate: the **per-origin consent strip** (nothing is requested from the network before **Allow these**), the **URL policy** (`http:`, local network and invalid addresses do not even generate a request), the **Privacy switches** (any origin, `http`, local network, server without CORS) and **Diagnostics**. **Rule to check at the end:** the image is never saved; the `mapping.json` only stores the URL.

**Setup.** In every step that types the URL, confirm with the Enter key (in a multi-line field Enter saves while the text has no line break; Shift+Enter breaks the line; with a line break in the text, leaving the field saves, without the trailing break). New folder `remotas` (folder project, as in R1). The package is `libraries/material3-compose/` (the **Image** type, Content layer; section 2). In this script, `PAGES` is the base of the app under test: on the preview, `https://fabianofranca.github.io/mapping/preview/`; on the main version, `https://fabianofranca.github.io/mapping/`. The test image is `PAGES` + `test-images/foto.png`: a 96 × 96 PNG with four quadrants (red, green, blue and yellow, from top to bottom and left to right), served by GitHub Pages with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. The canvas is drawn: check by screenshot and, to count, through the `.canvas-host`'s `data-component-images` (the remote photos actually drawn; the placeholder does not count). To know whether the app requested the image from the network, count the difference in `grep -c foto.png` in the server log before and after the step, when the URL is the local server's; for the `PAGES` URLs (R15.3 and R15.4) the log does not see the request (it goes out to GitHub Pages): count the Playwright `page.on('request')` events. **Local server** (R15.1): a Node server **without CORS** on port 8765 (`scripts/image-server.mjs`), which must run **on the same computer as Chrome** (a VM's `127.0.0.1` is not Chrome's). It logs each request in `servidor.log` (in the working folder), which the shell reads. If Chrome asks about local network access, accept (`accept_permission_prompt`).

| Step | Action | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |

On Chrome's computer, open the folder in Explorer and double-click `iniciar-servidor.cmd` **[person]** (or the double-click through the computer control); without Node on the computer, mark R15.8 to R15.11 "not run (no Node)" and warn the owner, who decides (security).
