Stop the server: open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/parar` in a Chrome tab. | **Screen:** **Privacy** goes back to the R15.2 state (no origin, four switches off). **Screen:** the `/parar` tab shows "stopped" and `http://127.0.0.1:8765/foto.png` stops opening. |

### R16 — Variants in code

**What it covers:** the Material 3 library stage (MD1): `variants` in the `code` of the `formatVersion` 9 specialization. An `enum` field (`style`) chooses the code variant (in Compose, it swaps the composable). The steps check the **already resolved** `code` in the MCP (`get_code_hints`, `get_annotation`, `get_marking`, `find_by_code`), the raw one in `get_specialization` and, in the app, the **Definition** and the variants table of the **Catalog**; R16.11 and R16.12 check the `slots` of a case with its own sheet (the library and `get_code_hints`). **Rule to check at the end:** no annotation `code` carries `variants` (in `get_code_hints`, the annotation's one in the `tree`); only the specialization's raw JSON and the `types` of `get_code_hints` do.

**Setup.** **Framing a piece (no gesture).** In "Frame X": select X in the **Tree**, press `Shift+2` (**Fit selection**) and, if there is not enough width, zoom with `Ctrl+=` or `Ctrl+-` with focus on the canvas; never arrows or dragging (they move the marking). **The Card in R25.8:** the Palette creates the Navigation bar over the Card, which by geometry becomes a child and follows the parent's Position change (documented behavior, #1087); the step puts the Card back at (30, 290) through the Details. Section 6 done; the requests to the MCP are made by the stdio client (appendix A). `ROOT` is the server's projects root (`design/mapeamentos` in section 6). The test script's specialization is small and goes inline: the shell writes it to `ROOT/mini-compose.json` in R16.1.

```json
{
  "format": "mapping-spec",
  "formatVersion": 9,
  "id": "mini-compose",
  "name": "Mini Compose",
  "version": 1,
  "platforms": [{ "id": "compose", "name": "Jetpack Compose", "language": "kotlin" }],
  "layers": [
    {
      "id": "components",
      "name": "Components",
      "color": "#1E88E5",
      "annotationTypes": [
        {
          "id": "button",
          "name": "Button",
          "fields": [
            { "key": "label", "type": "string", "required": true },
            {
              "key": "style",
              "type": "enum",
              "options": ["filled", "outlined", "text"],
              "default": "filled"
            }
          ],
          "code": {
            "compose": {
              "symbol": "androidx.compose.material3.Button",
              "path": "compose/material3/Button.kt",
              "params": { "label": "label" },
              "notes": "content = { Text(label) }",
              "variants": {
                "field": "style",
                "cases": {
                  "outlined": { "symbol": "androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedButton" },
                  "text": { "symbol": "androidx.compose.material3.TextButton" }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

| Step | Action | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R16.1 | **Write and validate the specialization.** In the shell, write the JSON above to `ROOT/mini-compose.json`. In the stdio client, `validate_specialization` with `path` `mini-compose.json`. | **Response:** no errors (the `path-without-repo` warning of `mini-compose` is expected); the `formatVersion` read is 9. |
| R16.2 | **Errors at the exact path.** In the stdio client, `validate_specialization` with `text` equal to the JSON, changing only the `text` case to `"purple"` (a value outside the `options`); then with `formatVersion` `8` and the rest the same. | **Response:** the 1st fails with an error at the path `layers[0].annotationTypes[0].code.compose.variants.cases.purple` saying that `"purple"` is not in the options of `"style"`; the 2nd fails with `only allowed with formatVersion 9` at the path `layers[0].annotationTypes[0].code.compose.variants`. |
| R16.3 | **Project and proposal.** In the stdio client, `create_project` with `path` `variants`, `name` `Variants` and `root` `design/mapeamentos`; then `propose_changes` in that project with a batch: `apply_specialization` (`file` `mini-compose.json`), `add_container` (`name` `Screen`, 360 × 800, `background` `#FFFFFF`: without `file`, the background is required), and, in it, two markings of type `mini-compose/button`: **Save** (`label` `Save`, `style` `filled`) and **Cancel** (`label` `Cancel`, `style` `outlined`), each with a `rect` (for example `{x: 20, y: 20, width: 140, height: 48}` and `{x: 180, y: 20, width: 140, height: 48}`) and a `create_annotation` of type `mini-compose/button` with those values. | **Response:** the project is created and the proposal comes back with an id, no error; `created` lists the container and the two markings. **Disk:** the `mapping.json` of `variants` still without a container or markings (the proposal does not write). |
| R16.4 | **Accept in the app.** Open the `variants` folder (**Open folder** `select_folder`), **Proposals** › **Review** the proposal, **Accept all changes**, **Apply accepted** and **Exit review**. | **Screen:** the **Screen** container with the **Save** and **Cancel** markings, each with a **Button** annotation; **Diagnostics** (`Ctrl+Shift+6`) with no error. **Disk:** the `mapping.json` stores `style` `filled` in one annotation and `outlined` in the other; `specs/mini-compose.json` exists with `formatVersion` 9. |
| R16.5 | **Resolved `get_code_hints`.** In the stdio client, `get_code_hints` of the **Save** and the **Cancel** markings (references from `list_markings`), `platform` `compose`. | **Response:** look at the **annotation's** `code` in the `tree` (not the one in `types`, which is the base's raw one): the `symbol` of **Save** is `androidx.compose.material3.Button` and that of **Cancel** is `androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedButton`; both with the `path` `compose/material3/Button.kt` (the case only swapped the `symbol`), the `param` `label` (`Save`/`Cancel`) and the `notes` `content = { Text(label) }`. The annotation's `code` does **not** carry `variants`; `types["mini-compose/button"]` is the raw one and does. |
| R16.6 | **`get_annotation` and `get_marking`.** In the stdio client, `get_annotation` of the **Cancel** annotation and `get_marking` of **Cancel** with `platform` `compose`. | **Response:** the `code.compose.symbol` is `androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedButton`, in `get_annotation` and in `get_marking`, without `variants`. |
| R16.7 | **`find_by_code` by variant.** In the stdio client, `find_by_code` with `symbol` `androidx.compose.material3.Button`; then with `androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedButton`; then with `path` `Button.kt`; finally with `symbol` `androidx.compose.material3.TextButton`. | **Response:** the 1st returns the **Button** type and **only** the **Save** annotation; the 2nd, **only** the **Cancel** one; the 3rd, **both**; the 4th returns the **Button** type with an **empty** annotation list (no annotation is on `text`). The type's `code` in all of them is the raw one, with `variants`. |
| R16.8 | **Raw specialization.** In the stdio client, `get_specialization` with `specId` = `mini-compose` in the `variants` project. | **Response:** the `code.compose` of **Button** carries `variants` with `field` `style` and the cases `outlined` and `text`, as in the file. |
| R16.9 | **Definition in the Details.** In the app, select **Cancel**, open **Details** (`Ctrl+Shift+3`) and read the **Definition** row; hover it and read the tooltip; repeat with **Save**. | **Screen:** the row shows "Jetpack Compose · Button.kt" in both; the **Cancel** tooltip carries the symbol `androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedButton`, the **Save** one carries `androidx.compose.material3.Button`. |
| R16.10 | **Variants table in the Catalog.** The test script's Mini Compose is a `.json` without components, so the project's **Catalog** does not list **Button**: in the shell, create the folder `mini-compose-package/` and copy the JSON from R16.1 to `mini-compose-package/mini-compose.spec.json`; on the home screen, click **Open library** (a real click, not by script: the picker requires the person's gesture) and choose the folder (`select_folder`); open the **Button** type and read the platform's code. | **Screen:** the base shows the `symbol` `androidx.compose.material3.Button` and the file `compose/material3/Button.kt`; below, the **Variants (style)** table with the rows `outlined` → `OutlinedButton` and `text` → `TextButton` (in the order of the `options`). |
| R16.11 | **Slots of a variants case: the library.** In the shell, `cp -r REPO/tests/fixtures/slots ROOT/slots-variants` and, with `node -e`, edit `ROOT/slots-variants/slots.spec.json`: `platforms` becomes `[{"id":"compose","name":"Compose","language":"kotlin"}]`; on the type `bar`, add the field `{"key":"style","type":"enum","options":["small","center"],"default":"small"}` and set `code.compose` to `{"symbol":"demo.Bar","path":"demo/Bar.kt","signature":"signatures/bar.compose.json","params":{"title":"title"},"slots":{"actions":"trailingContent"},"variants":{"field":"style","cases":{"center":{"symbol":"demo.CenterBar","path":"demo/CenterBar.kt","signature":"signatures/bar.center.compose.json","slots":{"navigationIcon":"leading"}}}}}`; on the type `pin`, set `code` to `{"compose":{"symbol":"demo.Pin","params":{"label":"label"}}}`. Then write two `mapping-signature` sheets in `ROOT/slots-variants/signatures/`, with the shape of `libraries/material3-compose/signatures/*.json` (`source` with `kind` `code`, `extractor` `agent`, `platform` `compose`, `language` `kotlin`, and the symbol and path above): `bar.compose.json` for `demo.Bar` (`demo/Bar.kt`) with a `value` parameter named title, `navigationIcon` and `trailingContent` (role `slot`); `bar.center.compose.json` for `demo.CenterBar` (`demo/CenterBar.kt`) with a `value` parameter named title, `leading` and `actions` (role `slot`). In the stdio client, `validate_library` with `path` `slots-variants`. | **Response:** `valid` `true`; no warning at a path under `variants.cases.center.slots` (the base's `actions` → `trailingContent`, which the `center` sheet lacks, is not inherited and does not warn). |
| R16.12 | **Slots of a variants case: `get_code_hints`.** In the stdio client, `create_project` with `path` `slots-variants-demo`, `name` `Slots variants` and `root` `design/mapeamentos`; then `propose_changes` on it with `apply_specialization` (`file` `slots-variants/slots.spec.json`), `add_container` (`name` `Slots`, `width` 400, `height` 300, `background` `#DDEEFF`) and, in it, a **Bar** (`style` `small`) and a **Center bar** (`style` `center`), each with a pin in the `navigationIcon` slot and one in the `actions` slot (`inside` the bar + `slot`, without `rect`, like R28.16). In the app, **Open folder** `slots-variants-demo`, **Proposals** (`Ctrl+Shift+7`) › **Review**, **Accept all changes**, **Apply accepted**; wait for **Saved**. Then `get_code_hints` (`platform` `compose`) of the **Center bar** and of the **Bar**. | **Response (Center bar):** the annotation's `symbol` is `demo.CenterBar` and its slot arguments are `{ name: "leading", slot: "navigationIcon" }` and `{ name: "actions", slot: "actions" }` (the case's own slot, and the base's `trailingContent` not inherited, so the argument is named by the slot's `id`). **Response (Bar):** the symbol is `demo.Bar` and the slot arguments are `{ name: "navigationIcon", slot: "navigationIcon" }` and `{ name: "trailingContent", slot: "actions" }`. |

### R17 — Material 3 library (Compose)

**What it covers:** the Material 3 library stage (MD5): the ready-made package `libraries/material3-compose/` (50 types, `formatVersion` 18, Jetpack Compose only), delivered in `examples/material3-compose.zip`. The steps check the zip and the package through the MCP (`validate_library`), applying the zip in the app (**Apply zip…**), the mapping of a contacts screen made only with the library (Scaffold, Top app bar, LazyColumn with two List items, an `outlined` Button and a FAB) through an MCP proposal and, at the end, that the agent reads the **screen tree with the right composable at each node**: `get_code_hints` returns `Scaffold` > `TopAppBar`, `LazyColumn` > `ListItem` ×2, `OutlinedButton` and `FloatingActionButton`, and the `outlined` variant swaps the symbol (`OutlinedButton`) without changing the file (`Button.kt`). MF5 (R17.22 to R17.30): the **Faithful** piece, read in the MCP's PNG (ImageMagick) and, in R17.30, in the app: the outlined `text-field` (gap with rounded corners), the elevated `card` (two shadows), the disabled `switch` (opaque), the number under the `time-picker` handle at 10:37, the `date-picker` with `today` and the `text` with no `color` on a `primary` `surface` (inherited color). MC6 (R17.31 to R17.34): the **Lines** piece: the `snackbar` of 1, 2 and 3 lines (48, 68 and 81), the `alert-dialog` with the buttons on two lines and, in the app, the `flow-row` wrapped by Arrange. Capture density (R17.39 and R17.40): the 174 × 120 `button` in a 3x container drawn by `render_marking` the same as the 58 × 40 one in a 1x container at `zoom` 3, the `component-overflow` of `plan_changes` with `update_container` `density` 3 and the `container-density` with 12. The `centered-hero` carousel (R17.41 and R17.42): the 3-item one at 360 wide with `itemSpacing` 8 drawn like Compose without `maxItemWidth`, the 264 big item from x 48 and the 40 small one at x 320, in the PNG of `render_marking` and, in proportion, in the app. The slider with 2000 steps (R17.43): without the ticks and without the `repeat limited` warning, a 4-high strip per segment, with the right colors in the PNG and, in proportion, in the app. The carousel label legible over the placeholder (R17.47): the 0.55 scrim leaves the `label` with a contrast of at least 4.5:1, in the PNG of `render_marking` (`575658`) and, in the app, in proportion (`202022`). Import by signature (S5, R17.44 to R17.46): the `button` with `shape` `small`, `horizontal` 12, `vertical` 4 and `containerColor` `tertiary` in `light` and `dark`, the `primary` `color` of the `divider` and the `subtitle` of the `small` `top-app-bar`, in the PNG of `render_marking`. In R17.7, the `outlined` case carries `calls.colors` `outlinedButtonColors`. Anchors and direction (R17.48 to R17.54, the Direction and anchor stage, `material3-compose` at version 15): the `tooltip` anchored to an `icon-button` with the 16 × 8 caret under the button's center, the `badge` on the corner of an `icon` (the 6 dot and the 16 counter, with the `BadgedBox` offsets), the `dropdown-menu` under a `text-field` (and `get_code_hints` with the side and alignment that each component's root declares) and the `rtl` screen (the back arrow and the chevron flipped, the search icon the same), in the PNG of `render_marking` and `render_container`, in `light` and in `dark`. Named slots (R17.55 to R17.57, `formatVersion` 17): the six types that declare slots (`bottom-app-bar`, `top-app-bar`, `scaffold`, `switch`, `swipe-to-dismiss` and `bottom-sheet`) drawn by `render_marking` with and without children, in `light` and in `dark`, and, in R17.6, the Scaffold's children read in the args of its slots (`topBar`, `content` and `floatingActionButton`). Accessibility (R17.58, `formatVersion` 18): the types that gained `<field>Description` fields and `iconDescription` columns draw the same, byte for byte. Inherited parameters (R17.60): the `center` case of the `top-app-bar` (`CenterAlignedTopAppBar`) does not inherit the base `subtitle` its sheet lacks, and the `small` case keeps it.

**Setup.** Section 6 done; the requests to the MCP are made by the stdio client (appendix A: `WS=<workspace> node scripts/testing/mcp-stdio-client.mjs calls.json`; arguments from `[{"list":true}]`). **Color box with `%@` (R17.19, R17.21, R17.41 and R17.42):** the commands measure the box on a 1 px row and carry `-bordercolor black -border 1` before the `-format`, because ImageMagick 6 (6.9.12, the cloud's) gets the box of a 1-row image wrong when the color touches the border (height 2 and wrong width, like `272x2+48+0`); with the 1 px black border, the box's `X` and `Y` count 1 more, and the expected values already come that way. `ROOT` is the server's projects root (`design/mapeamentos` in section 6) and `REPO` is the clone of the Mapping repository, where `examples/material3-compose.zip` is. The package carries the Roboto font (`fonts/Roboto-Regular.woff2` and `Roboto-Medium.woff2`, with the OFL license next to them): the texts come out in Roboto. ### R18 — Specialization warnings

**What it covers:** the Specialization warnings stage (`formatVersion` 10): `notices` on the type, on the field and on the `table` column, with the four `kind` values (`removed`, `deprecated`, `diverges`, `pending`). The steps check the refusal in a v9, the MCP (`notices.new` of `propose_changes` and `plan_changes`, `notices` of `get_specialization` and `get_code_hints`), the proposal review (still acceptable), the badge in the type picker and in the **Catalog**, the **Details** (no notices), the **Notices** window (`Ctrl+Shift+8`, only accessibility), the absence of **Notices: N** in the status bar, the update with only changed notices and (R18.14) the `pending` notices that the signature importer writes into the Material 3 library. **Rule to check at the end:** a notice only informs: nothing was blocked and **Incomplete** did not get a row for a notice.

**Setup.** Section 6 done (the test repository and `mapping-mcp.js`); the requests to the MCP are made by the stdio client (appendix A: `WS=<workspace> node scripts/testing/mcp-stdio-client.mjs calls.json`; arguments from `[{"list":true}]`). `ROOT` is the server's projects root (`design/mapeamentos` in section 6). The specialization of this test script is small and goes inline: the shell writes it to `ROOT/avisos.json` in R18.1.

```json
{
  "format": "mapping-spec",
  "formatVersion": 10,
  "id": "avisos-demo",
  "name": "Notices Demo",
  "version": 1,
  "platforms": [
    {
      "id": "demo",
      "name": "Demo",
      "language": "kotlin",
      "repo": { "url": "https://example.com/demo" }
    }
  ],
  "layers": [
    {
      "id": "ui",
      "name": "UI",
      "color": "#1E88E5",
      "annotationTypes": [
        {
          "id": "legacy",
          "name": "Legacy",
          "code": { "demo": { "symbol": "Legacy" } },
          "notices": [
            { "kind": "removed", "message": "Removed from the contract; use Card." }
          ],
          "fields": [{ "key": "heading", "type": "string" }]
        },
        {
          "id": "card",
```

### R19 — Roles in the link

**What it covers:** the Roles and external documents stage (PD1 to PD4 and PD6, `formatVersion` 11, schema v14): `allowedChildren` with a `{ layer, groups }` clause, `groups`, `childRoles` and `childRolesLabel` on the owner and `parentRole` on the annotation; in steps R19.26 to R19.29, the Link in the same layer stage (`formatVersion` 13, schema v15: the chain by role, the refused cycle and the nested `get_code_hints`). The steps check the specialization's validation, the **Link to …** dialog, the role `Select`, the `missing-role` and `unknown-role` pending items (**Incomplete** badge, **Incomplete** window), the owner change, a proposal with `parentRole`, the MCP over stdio (`role`, `linkedByRole`, `plan_library_update`) and the migration of the roles (stage #557, `formatVersion` 12: `rename-role`, `remove-role` and `set-role`). R19.30 to R19.35 (stage hug-fill-copy-field, `formatVersion` 19): the `copy-field` migration step with `when` (validation, refusal in 18, `plan_library_update`, the app's update and its **Undo**, `update_specialization` in a proposal). **Rule to check at the end:** a role pending item only informs: nothing is blocked by it (neither saving nor applying a proposal); it appears as the "Incomplete: N issue(s)" box in the annotation's Details and as a list only in the **Incomplete** window.

**Setup.** Section 6 done (the test repository and `mapping-mcp.js`); the requests to the MCP are made by the stdio client (appendix A: `WS=<workspace> node scripts/testing/mcp-stdio-client.mjs calls.json`; arguments from `[{"list":true}]`). `ROOT` is the server's projects root (`design/mapeamentos`); `create_project` takes `root` `design/mapeamentos`, because the server has two roots. The shell writes the small specialization to `ROOT/papeis.json` in R19.1, and the update steps (R19.20 onward) derive variants of it with `jq` (version 2 and 3, `formatVersion` 12 and `migrations`). Button accepts the events of the **Interaction** group and has the roles **Click** and **Hold** (label **Trigger**); Link accepts the whole **Events** layer, with no roles; Chip accepts only `track`, by id. The annotations appear as "Type · name" (for example **Button · Continue**).

### R20 — Document in an external repository

**What it covers:** the Roles and external documents stage (PD1, PD2, PD5 and PD6) and, from R20.19 on, the library documents (`documents`, `formatVersion` 21: `validate_library`, `get_library_document` and the **Documents** group of the Catalog, without and with the clone): the `doc` of a type as an object `{ repo, path }`, pointing to a `.md` in a repository declared in `docRepos` at the root of the specialization (`formatVersion` 11), and the project's `docRepos[<id>].localPath` (schema v14). The steps check the validation of the specialization and of the package through the MCP (`validate_specialization`, `validate_library` with and without `docClones`), the states of the **Document** section of the **Catalog** (folder connected and file found, the browser asks for confirmation, file missing, no folder, browser without a folder picker or without `urlTemplate`), the **Open in repository** link, the **Repositories** › **Documents** section of **Settings** (the **Local path of the root** field, which writes the `mapping.json`'s `docRepos`) and `get_component` with the document read from the clone or with `doc` `null` and `docExternal`. **Rule to check at the end:** the app made no network request to read a document (the CSP's `connect-src` is still `'none'`; the only contact with the repository address is the click on **Open in repository**, which this test script does not do) and no file of the clone was changed (`git status` clean).

**Setup.** Section 6 done (the test repository and `mapping-mcp.js`); the requests to the MCP are made by the stdio client (appendix A: `WS=<workspace> node scripts/testing/mcp-stdio-client.mjs calls.json`; arguments from `[{"list":true}]`). `WS` is the root of the test repository (the MCP server's working folder, where the `.mcp.json`, `design/mapeamentos/` and `assets/` are) and `ROOT` is `WS/design/mapeamentos`. The clone of the documents repository is in `WS/assets/design-docs/` (inside the server's `assets` root, and therefore also inside the working directory, the only place `get_component` reads an external document from). The repository address is fictitious (`gitlab.example.com`): nothing in the round reaches it. The specialization of this test script goes inline, in a package (folder) with an internal control document: the shell writes it to `WS/assets/docs-externos-pacote/docs-externos.spec.json` in R20.1. Four types show four situations: **Button** (document in the clone, `design-docs`), **Chip** (a document the clone does not have), **Popover** (repository `notas-internas`, with no `urlTemplate`) and **Badge** (internal document of the package, as a control).

```json
{
  "format": "mapping-spec",
  "formatVersion": 11,
  "id": "docs-externos",
  "name": "External Docs",
  "version": 1,
  "docRepos": [
    {
      "id": "design-docs",
      "url": "https://gitlab.example.com/group/design-docs",
      "urlTemplate": "https://gitlab.example.com/group/design-docs/-/blob/main/{path}",
      "ref": "main"
    },
    {
      "id": "notas-internas",
      "url": "https://gitlab.example.com/group/notas-internas"
    }
  ],
  "layers": [
    {
      "id": "componentes",
      "name": "Components",
      "color": "#1E88E5",
      "annotationTypes": [
        {
          "id": "button",
          "name": "Button",
          "doc": { "repo": "design-docs", "path": "components/button.md" },
          "fields": [{ "key": "texto", "type": "string", "required": true }]
        },
        {
          "id": "chip",
          "name": "Chip",
          "doc": { "repo": "design-docs", "path": "components/chip.md" },
          "fields": [{ "key": "texto", "type": "string" }]
        },
        {
          "id": "popover",
          "name": "Popover",
          "doc": { "repo": "notas-internas", "path": "docs/popover.md" },
          "fields": [{ "key": "texto", "type": "string" }]
        },
        {
          "id": "badge",
          "name": "Badge",
          "doc": "docs/badge.md",
          "fields": [{ "key": "texto", "type": "string" }]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The R20.1 shell builds the clone and the support folders like this (`WS` already exported):

```bash
cd "$WS"
mkdir -p assets/design-docs/components && cd assets/design-docs && git init -q
cat > components/button.md <<'EOF'
# Button

Button text coming from the external repository.

- First item
- Second item

![Button diagram](diagram.png)

See the [style guide](https://example.com/guide) and the [sibling file](link.md).
EOF
printf '# Link\n\nLink document.\n' > components/link.md
git add . && git -c user.email=test@example.com -c user.name=Test commit -qm "docs"
cd "$WS"
mkdir -p assets/design-docs-v2/components assets/notas-internas/docs assets/docs-externos-pacote/docs
printf '# Chip\n\nChip document.\n' > assets/design-docs-v2/components/chip.md
printf '# Popover\n\nPopover document, in the notas-internas clone.\n' > assets/notas-internas/docs/popover.md
printf '# Badge\n\nBadge document, inside the package.\n' > assets/docs-externos-pacote/docs/badge.md
```

### R21 — Workspace updated by the release

**What it covers:** the Workspace updated stage (WA1 and WA2): the `setup.sh` of `examples/workspace/` that each MCP release publishes together with `mapping-mcp.js`, the `SKILL.md` skill, the `AGENTS.mapping.md` block and `watch-comments.mjs` (the conversation watcher, which `setup.sh` installs at the workspace root), `watch-conversations.SKILL.md` (the `watch-conversations` skill, which `setup.sh` installs in `.agents/skills/watch-conversations/` with its `.claude/skills/` link) and `mapping-signature.mjs` (the signature extractor, which `setup.sh` installs in `tools/`) (each file with its `.sha256`). The steps check, against the **real release on GitHub**, the new workspace through the single line, the migration of the old workspace through the transition line (the old skeleton's `AGENTS.md` becomes the block between `mapping:begin` and `mapping:end`, with a backup and the "Para que servem" section intact), the `setup.sh` self-update and `--no-self-update`, the repeat with no change, the updated copy of the skill in `.claude/skills/`, the `sha256` check of every file before replacing any of them, the workspace server answering through the stdio client and, with a local server that imitates GitHub, the commit's `setup.sh` showing the reason for a download failure (HTTP 504 and 404) and using the assets API when the release's direct download answers 5xx (stage #877). It uses neither the app nor the browser.

**Setup.** Only shell and the MCP client over stdio (appendix A: `WS=<workspace> node scripts/testing/mcp-stdio-client.mjs calls.json`). `REPO` is the Mapping clone (recipe 1 of appendix A). Each step works in its own subfolder of `W21`. The `TAG` comes from the tester's message (the epic's release candidate); in a full round on `main`, it is the latest stable. R21 downloads from the **real** release, not from the local build: with no network to `github.com`, mark them all "not executed (no network to the release)"; if the release for `TAG` does not have `setup.sh`, mark them all "not executed (the release does not ship setup.sh)". `setup.sh`'s summary has the lines `Server:`, `Skill:`, `Watch skill:` (`installed`, `updated`, `no change` or a skip with a warning when the release has no such file), `AGENTS.md:` (this one says `created`, `updated`, `migrated`, `no change` or `not recognized…`) and `Watcher:` (`installed`, `updated`, `no change` or `not updated (release without the watcher)`); warnings go to stderr, which is why the output is saved with `2>&1`.

```bash
export W21=<work folder>/release-ws && mkdir -p "$W21" && cd "$W21"
# Directed round: TAG comes from the message. Full round on main: the latest stable.
TAG=$(basename "$(curl -fsSLI -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' https://github.com/fabianofranca/mapping/releases/latest)")
export TAG BASE="https://github.com/fabianofranca/mapping/releases/download/$TAG"
curl -fsSI "$BASE/setup.sh" > /dev/null && echo "release with setup.sh"
mkdir downloaded
for f in mapping-mcp.js setup.sh SKILL.md AGENTS.mapping.md watch-comments.mjs watch-conversations.SKILL.md mapping-signature.mjs; do
  curl -fsSL "$BASE/$f" -o "downloaded/$f" && curl -fsSL "$BASE/$f.sha256" -o "downloaded/$f.sha256"
done
(cd downloaded && sha256sum -c *.sha256)
# hash of every file in a folder (except .git), in order
snap() { (cd "$1" && find . -path ./.git -prune -o -type f -print0 | sort -z | xargs -0 sha256sum); }
```

R21.1 runs the release's `setup.sh` in an empty folder and checks the result:

```bash
cd "$W21" && mkdir ws-new && cd ws-new
curl -fsSL "$BASE/setup.sh" -o setup.sh && chmod +x setup.sh
./setup.sh "$TAG" > ../out-new.txt 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"; cat ../out-new.txt
(cd tools && sha256sum -c mapping-mcp.js.sha256)
node tools/mapping-mcp.js --version; node ../downloaded/mapping-mcp.js --version
cmp .agents/skills/spec-author/SKILL.md ../downloaded/SKILL.md
cmp watch-comments.mjs ../downloaded/watch-comments.mjs
cmp .agents/skills/watch-conversations/SKILL.md ../downloaded/watch-conversations.SKILL.md
test -L .claude/skills/watch-conversations && echo watch-link
(cd tools && sha256sum -c mapping-signature.mjs.sha256)
cmp tools/mapping-signature.mjs ../downloaded/mapping-signature.mjs
node tools/mapping-signature.mjs --help > /dev/null; echo "signature-exit=$?"
node watch-comments.mjs > ../out-watcher.txt 2>&1; echo "watcher-exit=$?"; cat ../out-watcher.txt
test -L .claude/skills/spec-author && echo link
grep -c 'mapping:begin' AGENTS.md; grep -c 'mapping:end' AGENTS.md
grep -n '^# Mappings\|^## What these mappings are for' AGENTS.md
```

R21.2 builds the old workspace from the Mapping repository's history (the `setup.sh` and the `AGENTS.md` from before the managed block) and runs the transition line, with `latest/download` replaced by `download/$TAG` and the tag passed to the script:

```bash
cd "$W21" && mkdir ws-old && cd ws-old
git -C "$REPO" show 05c1793:examples/workspace/AGENTS.md > AGENTS.md
git -C "$REPO" show 05c1793:examples/workspace/setup.sh > setup.sh && chmod +x setup.sh
mkdir -p projetos/demo && echo 'owner data' > projetos/demo/note.txt && echo '@AGENTS.md' > CLAUDE.md
python3 -I - <<'EOF'
import re
s = open('AGENTS.md', encoding='utf-8').read()
s = re.sub(r'<!--.*?-->', 'Document the screens of app X.', s, count=1, flags=re.S)
open('AGENTS.md', 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)
EOF
cp AGENTS.md ../AGENTS-before.md && sha256sum projetos/demo/note.txt CLAUDE.md > ../owner.sha256
curl -fsSL "$BASE/setup.sh" -o setup.sh && chmod +x setup.sh && ./setup.sh "$TAG" > ../out-old.txt 2>&1
echo "exit=$?"; cat ../out-old.txt
```

R21.2's check, in `ws-old`:

```bash
cmp setup.sh ../downloaded/setup.sh; ls AGENTS.md.bak-*; cmp AGENTS.md.bak-* ../AGENTS-before.md
cmp watch-comments.mjs ../downloaded/watch-comments.mjs
grep -c 'mapping:begin' AGENTS.md
[ "$(sed -n '/<!-- mapping:begin/,/<!-- mapping:end -->/p' AGENTS.md)" = "$(cat ../downloaded/AGENTS.mapping.md)" ] && echo block-same
section() { awk '/^## Para que servem/{f=1;next} /^## |<!-- mapping:begin/{f=0} f' "$1"; }
section ../AGENTS-before.md > ../section-before.txt; section AGENTS.md > ../section-new.txt
cmp ../section-before.txt ../section-new.txt; grep -c 'Document the screens of app X.' ../section-new.txt
grep -c '^## Structure' AGENTS.md
awk '/mapping:begin/{f=1} /mapping:end/{f=0} !f && /^## (Estrutura|Regras|Fluxo típico|Structure|Rules|Typical flow)/' AGENTS.md
sha256sum -c ../owner.sha256
```

R21.3 starts from a copy of `ws-new` with an old `setup.sh` (the release one with one extra line):

```bash
cd "$W21" && cp -a ws-new ws-stale && cd ws-stale
cp ../downloaded/setup.sh setup.sh && printf '\n# old version (R21)\n' >> setup.sh && cp setup.sh ../setup-stale.sh
./setup.sh "$TAG" > ../out-stale.txt 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"; cat ../out-stale.txt
cmp setup.sh ../downloaded/setup.sh
grep -c 'setup.sh updated' ../out-stale.txt; grep -c '^Server:' ../out-stale.txt
```

R21.4 and R21.5 repeat `setup.sh` in `ws-old`:

```bash
# R21.4
cd "$W21" && snap ws-old > before.txt
(cd ws-old && ./setup.sh "$TAG" > ../out-same.txt 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"; cat ../out-same.txt)
snap ws-old > after.txt && diff before.txt after.txt && echo same
ls ws-old/AGENTS.md.bak-*; grep -c 'setup.sh updated' out-same.txt
# R21.5
cd "$W21/ws-old"
rm .claude/skills/spec-author && mkdir -p .claude/skills/spec-author && echo old > .claude/skills/spec-author/SKILL.md
./setup.sh "$TAG" > ../out-copy.txt 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"
test -L .claude/skills/spec-author && echo link || echo real-folder
cmp .claude/skills/spec-author/SKILL.md ../downloaded/SKILL.md; cmp .agents/skills/spec-author/SKILL.md ../downloaded/SKILL.md
```

R21.6 and R21.7 (after R21.5, which leaves `ws-old` with the skill copy):

```bash
# R21.6: the old setup.sh from R21.3, without tools/
cd "$W21" && cp -a ws-new ws-lock && cd ws-lock && rm -rf tools
cp ../setup-stale.sh setup.sh && sha256sum setup.sh > ../lock-before.sha256
./setup.sh "$TAG" --no-self-update > ../out-lock.txt 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"; cat ../out-lock.txt
sha256sum -c ../lock-before.sha256; grep -c 'setup.sh updated' ../out-lock.txt
(cd tools && sha256sum -c mapping-mcp.js.sha256)
# R21.7: the release with one byte of the server corrupted
cd "$W21" && cp -a downloaded fake-release
python3 -I -c "p='fake-release/mapping-mcp.js'; d=bytearray(open(p,'rb').read()); d[len(d)//2]^=1; open(p,'wb').write(d)"
cp -a ws-old ws-tampered && snap ws-tampered > before-tampered.txt
(cd ws-tampered && MAPPING_RELEASE_BASE="file://$W21/fake-release" ./setup.sh > ../out-tampered.txt 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"; cat ../out-tampered.txt)
snap ws-tampered > after-tampered.txt && diff before-tampered.txt after-tampered.txt && echo same
ls ws-tampered/AGENTS.md.bak-*
```

R21.8, in `ws-new` (the client uses the skeleton's default command, `tools/mapping-mcp.js --root projects --root specializations`, so it does not need `.mcp.json`, which `setup.sh` does not create):

```bash
cd "$W21/ws-new"
cat > calls.json <<'EOF'
[{"name":"create_project","args":{"path":"demo","name":"Demo","root":"projects"}},{"name":"list_projects","args":{}}]
EOF
WS="$W21/ws-new" node "$REPO/scripts/testing/mcp-stdio-client.mjs" calls.json
node tools/mapping-mcp.js --version; ls projects/demo/mapping.json
```

R21.9 to R21.11 use the **commit's** `setup.sh` (`$REPO/examples/workspace/setup.sh`: the real release does not carry the fix yet) and a local server that imitates GitHub (`scripts/testing/mock-github-release.mjs`), with no network to `github.com`. The server serves the `downloaded` folder (or a copy of it), answers `504` on the direct download when asked and delivers the assets through the API; the first line of its output is the base URL, and the others are the requests:

```bash
# serve <folder> [server options] on a fresh copy of ws-new; ws=<name>, log in ../mock-<name>.txt
mock() { # $1 = name, $2 = release folder, rest = server options
  local n="$1" d="$2"; shift 2
  node "$REPO/scripts/testing/mock-github-release.mjs" "$d" "$@" > "$W21/mock-$n.txt" &
  MOCK_PID=$!; sleep 1; MOCK_BASE=$(head -1 "$W21/mock-$n.txt")
  cd "$W21" && rm -rf "ws-$n" && cp -a ws-new "ws-$n" && cp "$REPO/examples/workspace/setup.sh" "ws-$n/setup.sh" && rm -rf "ws-$n/tools"
}
# R21.9: 504 on the direct download, 200 on the assets API
cd "$W21" && mock r9 downloaded --direct 504
snap ws-r9 > before-r9.txt
(cd ws-r9 && MAPPING_GITHUB_BASE="$MOCK_BASE" MAPPING_GITHUB_API="$MOCK_BASE/api" ./setup.sh --no-self-update > ../out-r9.txt 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"); kill $MOCK_PID
cat out-r9.txt; (cd ws-r9/tools && sha256sum -c mapping-mcp.js.sha256)
grep -c 'releases/latest$' mock-r9.txt; grep -c 'releases/assets/' mock-r9.txt
# R21.10: 404 on both paths (the release without the server)
cd "$W21" && cp -a downloaded release-no-server && rm release-no-server/mapping-mcp.js release-no-server/mapping-mcp.js.sha256
mock r10 release-no-server && snap ws-r10 > before-r10.txt
(cd ws-r10 && MAPPING_GITHUB_BASE="$MOCK_BASE" MAPPING_GITHUB_API="$MOCK_BASE/api" ./setup.sh --no-self-update > ../out-r10.txt 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"); kill $MOCK_PID
cat out-r10.txt; snap ws-r10 > after-r10.txt && diff before-r10.txt after-r10.txt && echo same
grep -c '/api/' mock-r10.txt
# R21.11: 504 on both paths
cd "$W21" && mock r11 downloaded --direct 504 --api 504 && snap ws-r11 > before-r11.txt
(cd ws-r11 && MAPPING_GITHUB_BASE="$MOCK_BASE" MAPPING_GITHUB_API="$MOCK_BASE/api" ./setup.sh --no-self-update > ../out-r11.txt 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"); kill $MOCK_PID
cat out-r11.txt; snap ws-r11 > after-r11.txt && diff before-r11.txt after-r11.txt && echo same
```

| Step | Action | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |

### R22 — Comments: threads anchored to the mapping

**What it covers:** the Comments stage (CM1 to CM7), from the `mapping-thread` format (`docs/COMMENT-FORMAT.md`) to the conversation between the person and the agent: the identity in **Settings** and the state without an identity (the identity notice on touch, in **New conversation** and **Comment**); the **Comments** window (`Ctrl+Shift+0`), the filters and the status bar; the pins hidden on open and the **Conversations** and **Comment** buttons; the **Conversation** window (stacked under Details; every conversation opens there, and Details only lists the item's conversations) with the conversation on the item, on the field and on the loose point; `list_threads`, `get_thread`, `open_thread`, `post_message` with the `after` guard and `propose_changes` with `thread` (the proposal card); resolving and reopening; the citation (`@`, paste and the live chip), the **Cited in** and the orphan conversation; deleting one and in bulk; the zip, the project on this device and the file edited from outside. Each step checks the screen and the disk (`comments/` and `comments/resolved/`).

**Setup.** Section 6 done (test repository, `mapping-mcp.js` and `.mcp.json` with the root `design/mapeamentos`) and the stdio client from appendix A (`WS=<test repository> node scripts/testing/mcp-stdio-client.mjs calls.json`). The script's own folder is the repository's example, unzipped, with its three conversations (one waits for the human, on the **style** field of **Register**; one waits for the agent, on the **Save** marking; one resolved, on **Manage plan**). Without the MCP, mark the MCP steps "not executed (no MCP)". The `.canvas-host` publishes the number of drawn pins in `data-pins`.

```bash
export W22=<working folder>/r22 && mkdir -p "$W22"
export PROJ=<test repository>/design/mapeamentos/conversas
if [ -e "$PROJ" ]; then echo "$PROJ already exists: the setup already ran; do not run it again"
else mkdir -p "$PROJ" && unzip -q "$REPO/examples/full-example.zip" -d "$PROJ"; fi
cat > "$W22/estado.py" <<'PY'
import json, glob, os, sys
root = sys.argv[1]
for p in sorted(glob.glob(root + '/comments/**/*.json', recursive=True)):
    t = json.load(open(p, encoding='utf-8'))
    msgs = [(m['author']['kind'], m['author']['name'], m['text'][:28], m['proposal']) for m in t['messages']]
    print(os.path.relpath(p, root), t['id'][:8], t['anchor'], 'rev', t['revision'], 'resolved' if t['resolved'] else 'open', msgs)
PY
snap() { (cd "$PROJ" && find comments -type f -print0 | sort -z | xargs -0 sha256sum); }
estado() { python3 -I "$W22/estado.py" "$PROJ"; }
```

### R23 — Perspectives

**What it covers:** the Perspectives stage (PE1 to PE4): migrating a v15 project (`project.id`, `perspectives` and `arrivals`, with the backup in `backups/`); the main bar's picker, **New perspective…** and **Manage perspectives…**; sending and removing items (right-click menu and the **Perspectives** section of Details); dragging only changes the position in the open perspective; what is born in a perspective reaches Full (arrival area, the "Came from…" badge, the notice in Details, **Dismiss** and **Next one that came**); layers hidden per perspective; **For everyone** (in `mapping.json`) and **Only me** (in the browser's IndexedDB, by `project.id`); the "Full only" restrictions; the review that locks the picker; deleting a perspective (nothing leaves the project) and undoing; and the MCP reads (`get_project`, `get_perspective`, `get_marking`, `get_container`), which never writes.

**Setup.** Section 6 done (test repository, `mapping-mcp.js` and `.mcp.json` with the root `design/mapeamentos`) and the stdio client from appendix A (`WS=<test repository> node scripts/testing/mcp-stdio-client.mjs calls.json`). `S` is the `apoio/` folder and `REPO`, the Mapping clone (appendix A). The script's own folder `perspectivas` is born from a schema 15 `mapping.json` written by the shell (3 containers with no image, one marking in each, 2 arrows and 3 annotations in 2 layers). `idb` reads the "Only me" perspectives from the tab's IndexedDB. Without the MCP, mark R23.21 and R23.24 "not executed (no MCP)". **The block below runs only once, at the start:** the `v15.py` line rewrites the v15 `mapping.json` and, with the app open, produces "Project updated from outside." and one more backup in `backups/`. To redo R23, close the project and delete the `perspectivas` folder first.

```bash
export W23=<working folder>/r23 && mkdir -p "$W23"
export PROJ=<test repository>/design/mapeamentos/perspectivas
cat > "$W23/v15.py" <<'PY'
import json, os, sys
root = sys.argv[1]
T = '2026-11-07T12:00:00.000Z'
def cont(i, name, x):
    return {"id": i, "name": name, "file": None, "width": 400, "height": 300, "placement": {"x": x, "y": 0, "scale": 1},
            "parentId": None, "markingColor": None, "locked": False, "source": None, "background": "#FFFFFF"}
def mark(i, c, name):
    return {"id": i, "containerId": c, "parentId": None, "name": name, "rect": {"x": 20, "y": 20, "width": 200, "height": 100},
            "needsReview": False, "locked": False, "floating": False, "source": None}
def arrow(i, src, dst):
    return {"id": i, "from": src, "to": dst, "fromSide": "right", "toSide": "left", "points": [], "style": "straight", "name": None, "locked": False}
def note(i, m, layer, name, key, value):
    return {"id": i, "markingId": m, "layerId": layer, "name": name, "parentAnnotationId": None, "parentRole": None,
            "type": None, "values": None, "entries": [{"id": i + "e", "key": key, "value": value}]}
doc = {"schemaVersion": 15, "revision": 0, "app": "mapping", "coordinateSystem": "image-pixels-exif-oriented",
       "project": {"name": "Perspectives", "createdAt": T, "updatedAt": T}, "specializations": [], "platformRepos": {}, "docRepos": {},
       "layers": [{"id": "L1", "name": "Layer 1", "color": "#E53935", "spec": None}, {"id": "L2", "name": "Data", "color": "#1E88E5", "spec": None}],
       "containers": [cont("C1", "Screen A", 0), cont("C2", "Screen B", 500), cont("C3", "Screen C", 1000)],
       "markings": [mark("M1", "C1", "Button"), mark("M2", "C2", "List"), mark("M3", "C3", "Chart")],
       "arrows": [arrow("S1", "M1", "M2"), arrow("S2", "M2", "M3")],
       "annotations": [note("A1", "M1", "L1", "Action", "route", "/buy"), note("A2", "M2", "L2", "Source", "table", "orders"), note("A3", "M3", "L2", "Metric", "series", "sales")]}
os.makedirs(root, exist_ok=True)
open(os.path.join(root, "mapping.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8").write(json.dumps(doc, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n")
PY
if [ -e "$PROJ" ]; then echo "$PROJ already exists: the setup already ran; do not run it again"
else python3 -I "$W23/v15.py" "$PROJ" && cp "$PROJ/mapping.json" "$W23/original.json"; fi
cat > "$W23/estado.py" <<'PY'
import json, sys
d = json.load(open(sys.argv[1] + '/mapping.json', encoding='utf-8'))
names = {c['id']: c['name'] for c in d['containers']} | {m['id']: m['name'] for m in d['markings']}
label = lambda r: names.get(r) or r[:8]
print('schema', d['schemaVersion'], 'rev', d['revision'], 'id', d['project'].get('id', '-')[:8], '| containers', len(d['containers']), 'markings', len(d['markings']), 'arrows', len(d['arrows']), 'annotations', len(d['annotations']))
print(' pl', [(label(c['id']), c['placement']['x'], c['placement']['y']) for c in d['containers']])
for p in d.get('perspectives', []):
    print(' P', p['name'], '| hidden', p['hiddenLayers'], '| items', [(label(i['root']), i['x'], i['y']) for i in p['items']])
print(' arrivals', [(label(a['root']), a['fromName']) for a in d.get('arrivals', [])])
PY
cat > "$W23/idb.mjs" <<'JS'
const { connect } = await import(`${process.env.REPO}/scripts/testing/cloud.mjs`);
const { page } = await connect(process.env.S);
const output = await page.evaluate(async () => {
  if (!(await indexedDB.databases()).some((b) => b.name === 'mapping-perspectivas')) return {};
  const db = await new Promise((ok, fail) => { const r = indexedDB.open('mapping-perspectivas'); r.onsuccess = () => ok(r.result); r.onerror = () => fail(r.error); });
  const out = {};
  if (db.objectStoreNames.contains('perspectives')) {
    const st = db.transaction('perspectives').objectStore('perspectives');
    const keys = await new Promise((ok) => { const q = st.getAllKeys(); q.onsuccess = () => ok(q.result); });
    for (const k of keys) out[k.slice(0, 8)] = await new Promise((ok) => { const q = st.get(k); q.onsuccess = () => ok(q.result.map((p) => p.name)); });
  }
  db.close();
  return out;
});
console.log(JSON.stringify(output));
process.exit(0);
JS
estado() { python3 -I "$W23/estado.py" "$PROJ"; }
snap() { sha256sum "$PROJ/mapping.json"; }
idb() { node "$W23/idb.mjs"; }
```

### R25 — Faithful components

**What it covers:** the Faithful components stage (CF1 to CF12, `formatVersion` 4 of the **component** and 15 of the **specialization**, schema v19, the epic's MCP): the stroke (`stroke.cap`, `join`, `sides`, the root's clip with the `outside` stroke and the shadow), the layout (CF2), the text (CF3), `runs` and the chip (CF4), the tokens (CF5), the **Drawing mode** (CF6), the icons (CF7), the image in the MCP (CF9), the drawing proof and the `operationsFile` (CF10), the `import_measured` op (CF11) and the aligned overlay, the slot's `clip` and the warning on `none` (CF12). The steps check, through `validate_library`, the test library and the version rule, and, through PNG crops of the canvas and the MCP's PNG, the drawing. **Rule to check at the end:** `mapping.json` stores nothing of the drawing. Afterwards: EX3 (R25.75 to R25.78), MF2 (R25.79 to R25.82), MF3 (R25.83 to R25.86), MF5 (R25.87 to R25.90), MC0 to MC4 (R25.91 to R25.98) and CF12 (R25.99 to R25.107: the aligned overlay of `none`, the slot's `clip` and the `content larger than the box` warning on the `none` parent, stage layout-flex-grid) and CF13 (R25.108 to R25.116: the `grid` with `span`, `minColumnWidth`, `repeat.layout` with equal columns and `hug`, the `weight`s and the validation messages, same stage) and CF14 (R25.117 to R25.120: `min-content` and `max-content` in `width`/`height` and in `sizing`, the `max-content` `row` that does not wrap, `fit_marking` and the refusal of version 3, same stage), and HC5 (R25.131 to R25.135: a `fill` label inside a `hug` frame, measured by its content, in the `m3-hug` and `m3-hug2` libraries: the widths 96, the content and 136, the sum of two `fill` labels, `fit_marking`, the creation without `rect` and Arrange, equal in the app and in the MCP's PNG, stage hug-fill-copy-field), and VL1 (R25.121 to R25.125: the `let` and `$var` variables of the `formatVersion` 4 component, swapped at read time, with the errors of name, of undefined variable, of cycle, of type at the point of use and of version, and the card with variables drawn the same in the MCP's PNG and in the app, stage variaveis-formato-4), equal in the app and in the MCP's PNG.

**Setup.** Section 6 done (the test repository and `mapping-mcp.js`); the requests to the MCP are made by the stdio client (appendix A: `WS=<workspace> node scripts/testing/mcp-stdio-client.mjs calls.json`; arguments from `[{"list":true}]`). `ROOT` is the server's projects root (`design/mapeamentos` in section 6) and `REPO` is the clone of the Mapping repository, where `libraries/material3-compose/` is. The test library `m3-fiel` is a copy of the Material 3 (Compose) package in which the shell swaps thirteen components (from `divider` to `chip` and, up to MC4, `badge`, `snackbar`, `top-app-bar`, `button` and `flow-row`) for minimal versions in `formatVersion` 4; the repository's `scripts/testing/fiel.mjs` writes them (`node REPO/scripts/testing/fiel.mjs <library folder> [formatVersion]`; the second argument is the `formatVersion`, `4` or `3`; do not write a script in its place):

The Divider (140 × 140, white background) has three horizontal bars with a red `#B3261E` stroke (width 12, the line goes from x 12 to x 88 and each bar's center is at y 10, 40 and 70), with `cap` `butt`, `round` and `square`; and, below, three L-shaped corners (width 16, the vertex at x 14, y 14 of the 40 × 40 frame, at x 5, 50 and 95 and y 90 of the Divider), with `join` `miter`, `round` and `bevel`. The Text field (240 × 56) is an `#E6E0E9` rectangle with a purple `#6750A4` stroke of 3, inside, only at the bottom (`sides` `["bottom"]`). The Card (200 × 100) is white with a green `#1B5E20` ring of 8 **outside** (`align` `outside`) on the component's root. The layout pieces (CF2), on a white background: the **List item** (240 × 120) has a brown `#6D4C41` ruler of 200 × 6 and, below, a light-blue `#4FC3F7` card **`hug` on both axes** (`padding` 8) with a `fill` text ("Quando o cartão abraça o texto longo", font 14, line height 20); R25.9 says what to expect. The **Navigation bar** (240 × 180) has a `repeat` of the `items` field with `distribute` `"fill"` and `gap` 10 in a column with `padding` 10: each row has the color of the `label` column (`A` pink `#D81B60`, `B` yellow `#F9A825`, `C` teal `#00897B`), and the rows split the height equally (R25.10); the `items` field is born **empty** in the app (the `preview` does not fill a table), and R25.8 adds the three rows. The **Checkbox** (240 × 60) has a row with `gap` 10 and `padding` 10 and two `fill` rectangles side by side, the left one purple `#8E24AA` with `maxWidth` 60 and the right one orange `#FB8C00`: both 40 tall (R25.11 says what to expect). The **Text** (110 × 142, white background, `padding` 5, `gap` 4), from CF3: an orange `#E65100` ruler of 100 × 4, a blue `#0D47A1` **line** ("Oi supercalifragilisticoexpialidocioso demais", box of 100 × 20, `wrap` `"none"` and `ellipsis`: a single line, ending in `…`), a purple `#4A148C` **paragraph** ("Um dois tres quatro cinco seis sete oito nove dez", box of 100 × 60, `ellipsis` and `maxLines` from the type's `maxLines` field, with 2 as the default) and a black **loose** text ("Texto solto", with no `maxLines` or `ellipsis`, `height` `fill`, which takes what is left of the height: 36). The **Chip** (260 × 116, white background, `padding` 10, `gap` 8), from CF4's rich text, uses the type's `label` field (the `preview` gives `novo`). An olive `#827717` ruler of 240 × 4; a **line** (v from 22 to 48; font 14, line height 20, node color `#455A64`) with four runs: `Mmmm ` in the node color, `Mmmm` in **bold** (`weight` 700) and green `#2E7D32`, a space and the **chip** (the `label` field's text, white, cyan `#00ACC1` background, `radius` 8, `padding` `[3, 6]`): the box is 26 tall and its width is the text's plus 12; and a **break** (v from 56 to 102; box 100 wide, node color wine `#880E4F`) with `WWWWWW` and a second chip, lime `#C0CA33`, with the text ` novo` (**with a leading space**) in black, which does not fit in the rest of the line above and goes **whole** to the second one (R25.19). The **measuring helpers** (ImageMagick, in the shell; PNG crops with `deviceScaleFactor` 1): `tinta <png> <color>` prints the ink box of the color as `WxH+X+Y` (in screen pixels; it is the union of the color's blotches larger than 300 pixels, so that a point or the antialiasing does not stretch the box; for thin text, run with `AREA=4 tinta …`; `FUZZ=<n>` replaces the color's 6% threshold, and the text cut at the edge in R25.73 uses `FUZZ=55 AREA=1`, which includes the antialiasing grays), and `sonda <png> <X0> <Y0> <s> <u> <v>` prints the color (hexadecimal; compare the first 6 digits) of the pixel at (X0 + u·s, Y0 + v·s), where `u` and `v` are **component units** and `s` is screen pixels per unit:

```bash
tinta() { convert "$1" -fuzz ${FUZZ:-6}% -fill '#ff00ff' -opaque "$2" -fuzz 0 -fill black +opaque '#ff00ff' -fill white -opaque '#ff00ff' -define connected-components:area-threshold=${AREA:-300} -define connected-components:verbose=true -connected-components 8 null: 2>/dev/null | awk '$NF ~ /gray\(255\)|white|srgb\(255,255,255\)/ {split($2,a,/[x+]/); w=a[1];h=a[2];x=a[3];y=a[4]; if(n++==0){x0=x;y0=y;x1=x+w;y1=y+h}else{if(x<x0)x0=x;if(y<y0)y0=y;if(x+w>x1)x1=x+w;if(y+h>y1)y1=y+h}} END{if(n)printf "%dx%d+%d+%d\n",x1-x0,y1-y0,x0,y0}'; }
sonda() { convert "$1" -format "%[hex:p{$(awk "BEGIN{printf \"%d,%d\", $2+$4*$5, $3+$4*$6}")}]\n" info:; }
medir() { read W H X Y < <(tinta "$1" "$2" | tr 'x+' '  '); s=$(awk "BEGIN{print $W/$3}"); X0=$(awk "BEGIN{print $X-($4)*$s}"); Y0=$(awk "BEGIN{print $Y-($5)*$s}"); echo "H/W=$(awk "BEGIN{print $H/$W}") s=$s"; }
unid() { tinta "$1" "$2" | tr 'x+' '  ' | awk -v s="$s" '{printf "W=%.1f H=%.1f\n", $1/s, $2/s}'; }
medirsel() { read X0 Y0 W _ <<<"$1"; s=$(awk "BEGIN{print $W/$2}"); echo "s=$s"; }
caixa() { read CL CA CX CY < <(tinta "$1" "$2" | tr 'x+' '  '); echo "corner u=$(awk "BEGIN{print ($CX-$X0)/$s}") v=$(awk "BEGIN{print ($CY-$Y0)/$s}")"; }
```

`medir <png> <color> <width> <u> <v>` finds the color's ink, computes `s` (the ink's width in pixels divided by `<width>`, the expected width in units) and the component's origin in pixels (`X0`, `Y0`), knowing that the ink's top-left corner is at (`<u>`, `<v>`) units, and prints the `H/W` ratio and `s`. `medirsel "<data-selection-box>" <width>` does the same without looking at the color, for the piece whose color is almost the canvas's background (`#CFD8DC`, `#E0E0E0`: with `-fuzz 6%` it matches the background and `medir` gets it wrong): with the marking selected, read the `.canvas-host`'s `data-selection-box` (`"left top width height"`, in crop pixels) **before** `Esc` and pass it in quotes with the marking's width in units; it defines `s` and gives `X0`/`Y0` (the marking's (0, 0) corner). `unid <png> <color>` prints the ink's width `W` and height `H` **in units**, with the `s` of the last `medir`. `caixa <png> <color>` stores the ink's box in `CL CA CX CY` (width, height and top-left corner, in pixels) and prints the corner in units (`u` and `v`, with the `s`, `X0` and `Y0` of the last `medir`); then, `sonda <png> $CX $CY $s <u> <v>` probes from that box's corner (for example, a chip's), with `u` and `v` in units, and `CL/s` is its width in units.

Each crop comes from Playwright/CDP, at 1280×720 and `deviceScaleFactor` 1, `page.screenshot({ path, clip })` with the `clip` equal to the `.canvas-host` box (`boundingBox()`), with focus on the canvas (`page.locator('main[data-canvas-area]').focus()`) and **Esc** (no marking selected) and with the mouse outside the canvas. With focus on a button in Details, Esc closes the window instead of clearing the selection. The crop is always also looked at by eye; the measurement only confirms.

**Warnings of this script's libraries.** The `m3-*` libraries are copies of the Material 3 (Compose) package, which validates with `errors` `[]` and `warnings` `[]`, and in the package window with "0 error(s) and 0 warning(s)." (a library of this script that a step draws with a test piece may add the warnings that step names). Where a step says "no error and no warning", this is what it means: **any warning, or any error, fails**; the check is `errors` and `warnings` empty and, in the package's window, "0 error(s) and 0 warning(s).". What the swapped pieces write by hand does not generate a new warning.

**Library with tokens (CF5).** The repository's `scripts/testing/tokens.mjs` turns a copy of the Material 3 package into `m3-tokens`: it ensures the specialization is at `formatVersion` 15 or more (`Math.max(spec.formatVersion, 15)`: the package is already at 17 and stays there, because the named slots ask for 17 and `fieldModels` and the signatures for 16) and **merges** four values into the package's `tokens` (`modes` `["light", "dark"]`): `primary` and `on-primary` per mode (the same as the package's) and simple `radius-md` and `space-4`, and swaps the `card` for a `formatVersion` 4 component that reads those tokens with `{ "$token": … }` (background, radius, padding and an `on-primary` sample) and brings four text lines of 10 letters: `iiiiiiiiii` and `WWWWWWWWWW` **without `family`** (the default font: the `font-sans` token) and the same two with `family` `{ "$token": "font-mono" }`, plus a yellow `#FFEB3B` ruler 100 wide for `medir`. With the second argument `error`, the `card` comes out with two defective nodes (a `fill` with a nonexistent token and a `cornerRadius` with a color token).

**CF12 library (R25.99).** The `node -e` that swaps four components of the `ROOT/m3-alinh` copy of `m3-tokens` (`ROOT` goes literally in the command, as in the other shell blocks):

```bash
node -e "const fs=require('fs');const W='ROOT/m3-alinh/components/';const cellOf=(a,j,c,r)=>({type:'frame',name:'cell',width:50,height:50,anchors:{left:50*c,top:50*r},layout:{type:'none',align:a,justify:j},children:[{type:'rect',name:'mark',width:10,height:10,fill:'#B3261E'}]});const strip=(x,a,j)=>({type:'frame',name:'strip',width:50,height:50,anchors:{left:x,top:150},layout:{type:'none',align:a,justify:j},children:[{type:'frame',name:'piece',width:'hug',height:'hug',fill:'#1565C0',children:[{type:'rect',width:10,height:10,fill:'none'}]}]});const P=['start','center','end'];const cells=[];P.forEach((a,r)=>P.forEach((j,c)=>cells.push(cellOf(a,j,c,r))));cells.push(strip(0,'stretch','stretch'),strip(50,'stretch','end'),strip(100,'start','start'));const w=(id,name,size,template)=>fs.writeFileSync(W+id+'.json',JSON.stringify({format:'mapping-component',formatVersion:4,id,name,size,template}));w('card','Card',{width:150,height:200},{type:'frame',fill:'#ECEFF1',layout:{type:'none'},children:cells});const boxOf=(id,name,clip)=>w(id,name,{width:200,height:160},{type:'frame',fill:'#ECEFF1',layout:{type:'none'},children:[{type:'slot',name:'content',fill:'#B0BEC5',anchors:{left:20,right:20,top:20},height:60,clip}]});boxOf('box','Box',true);boxOf('lazy-column','LazyColumn',false);w('spacer','Spacer',{width:120,height:40},{type:'frame',fill:'#E65100'})"
```

**CF13 library (R25.108).** The `node -e` that swaps four components of the `ROOT/m3-grade` copy of `m3-tokens` (`ROOT` goes literally in the command; the JS goes between apostrophes and only uses double quotes, because of the `$` in `$rows` and `$field`). The `card` is a 3-column grid (`gap` and `lineGap` 10, `padding` 10) with five bars of height 20 and `span` 2 on the first, the third and the fourth; the `box`, a `minColumnWidth` 120 grid with `gap` and `lineGap` 8 and seven bars; the `lazy-column`, a `row` with three `fill` bars of `weight` 1, 2 and 1; the `navigation-bar`, a `repeat` of the `items` field in a `grid` `layout` with `columns` `{ "$rows": "items" }` and `width` `"hug"`, with each segment cyan `#4FC3F7` and the `label` column's text. Since the swapped `navigation-bar` does not draw the `interaction`, the script removes that field (and the examples that use it) from the type in the specialization, as `tokens.mjs` does with the `card`; and gives the component a `preview` with two rows in `items` (without them the default table is empty, `{ "$rows": "items" }` is worth 0 and the validator warns `invalid value in layout.columns: 0`):

```bash
node -e '
const fs=require("fs");const W="ROOT/m3-grade/components/";
const w=(id,name,size,template)=>fs.writeFileSync(W+id+".json",JSON.stringify({format:"mapping-component",formatVersion:4,id,name,size,template}));
const r=(name,fill,extra)=>Object.assign({type:"rect",name,height:20,fill},extra);
w("card","Card",{width:160,height:100},{type:"frame",fill:"#ECEFF1",layout:{type:"grid",columns:3,gap:10,lineGap:10,padding:10},children:[r("a","#B3261E",{span:2}),r("b","#1565C0"),r("c","#1B5E20",{span:2}),r("d","#E65100",{span:2}),r("e","#4A148C")]});
w("box","Box",{width:400,height:76},{type:"frame",fill:"#ECEFF1",layout:{type:"grid",minColumnWidth:120,gap:8,lineGap:8},children:[1,2,3,4,5,6,7].map((i)=>r("c"+i,"#1565C0"))});
const p=(name,fill,weight)=>({type:"rect",name,fill,weight});
w("lazy-column","LazyColumn",{width:200,height:30},{type:"frame",layout:{type:"row"},children:[p("p1","#B3261E",1),p("p2","#1565C0",2),p("p3","#1B5E20",1)]});
w("navigation-bar","Navigation bar",{width:300,height:60},{type:"frame",fill:"#FFFFFF",layout:{type:"column",padding:10},children:[{type:"repeat",name:"segments",field:"items",width:"hug",layout:{type:"grid",columns:{"$rows":"items"},gap:4},template:{type:"frame",name:"segment",fill:"#4FC3F7",layout:{type:"row",padding:4},children:[{type:"text",name:"label",text:{"$field":"label"},color:"#000000"}]}}]});
const nb=W+"navigation-bar.json";const c=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(nb,"utf8"));c.preview={items:[{label:"A",icon:"",selected:"false"},{label:"B",icon:"",selected:"false"}]};fs.writeFileSync(nb,JSON.stringify(c));
const sf=W+"../material3-compose.spec.json";const sp=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(sf,"utf8"));for(const l of sp.layers)for(const t of l.annotationTypes)if(t.id==="navigation-bar"){t.fields=t.fields.filter((f)=>f.key!=="interaction");t.examples=t.examples.filter((e)=>(e.values||{}).interaction===undefined)}fs.writeFileSync(sf,JSON.stringify(sp))
'
```

#### R25.126 to R25.130 — The test tooltip and the `$anchor.*` (R3 of the Direction and anchor stage)

**What it covers:** the `anchor` on the component's root (`formatVersion` 4) and the five `$anchor.*` pseudo-fields: a test tooltip whose arrow changes side with `$anchor.side` and falls under the center (or beside the middle) of the anchor with `$anchor.x` and `$anchor.y`, on the **four sides**, in the MCP's PNG and in the app, and the version and name errors. The direction is `ltr` (the project's); `rtl` belongs to R27.

**Setup.** Section 6 done (the test repository and `mapping-mcp.js`); `ROOT` is the server's projects root (`design/mapeamentos`), `REPO` the repository clone and the requests to the MCP go through the stdio client (appendix A). The `node -e` swaps the `card` of the `m3-ancora` copy for an 80 × 40 **test tooltip** (`#1565C0`) with an 8 × 8 square arrow (`#E65100`) on the edge facing the anchor (the base, in `top`; the top, in `bottom`; the right edge, in `start`; the left one, in `end`), placed by `$anchor.x` (or `$anchor.y`) minus 4, and with `anchor` on the root (`top`, `center`, `main` 8):

```bash
node -e '
const fs=require("fs");const L="ROOT/m3-ancora/";
const x4={"$sub":[{"$field":"$anchor.x"},4]},y4={"$sub":[{"$field":"$anchor.y"},4]};
const sw=(cases,def)=>({"$switch":"$anchor.side",cases,default:def});
const card={format:"mapping-component",formatVersion:4,id:"card",name:"Card",size:{width:80,height:40},
 anchor:{side:"top",align:"center",offset:{main:8,cross:0}},
 template:{type:"frame",name:"raiz",fill:"#1565C0",layout:{type:"none"},children:[
  {type:"rect",name:"seta",width:8,height:8,fill:"#E65100",
   anchors:{left:sw({top:x4,bottom:x4,start:72,end:0},36),top:sw({top:32,bottom:0,start:y4,end:y4},16)}}]}};
fs.writeFileSync(L+"components/card.json",JSON.stringify(card));
'
```

The `Screen` container of R25.127 is 400 × 300 and the target, `Target`, takes up `{ x: 180, y: 130, width: 40, height: 40 }` (center at 200, 150). Each tooltip is born **with no `rect`**, at the size of 80 × 40 and snapped by the component's default: above (`top`: at `(160, 82)`), below (`bottom`: `(160, 178)`), on the left (`start`, in `ltr`: `(92, 130)`) and on the right (`end`: `(228, 130)`). Each one's arrow sits, in container coordinates: `top` at `(196..204, 114..122)`, `bottom` at `(196..204, 178..186)`, `start` at `(164..172, 146..154)` and `end` at `(228..236, 146..154)`.

#### R25.131 to R25.135 — A `fill` label in a `hug` frame (HC5 of the stage hug-fill-copy-field)

**What it covers:** a `fill` child on the main axis of a `hug` frame measured by its content. The test **menu item** is the `chip` of the `m3-hug` copy, a `formatVersion` 4 component with a `hug` root (`minWidth` 96, `maxWidth` 136, `row`, padding 8 × 12, gap 8), a fixed 24 × 24 icon (`#6750A4`) and a `fill` label (14 px, one line, with an ellipsis); the root is `#EEEEEE`. The width is the padding (24), the icon (24), the gap (8) and the label, between 96 and 136: label `Ok` gives **96** (the minimum), `Settings` gives **107** (its content) and a 40-letter label gives **136** (the maximum, with the label cut by the ellipsis). The `m3-hug2` copy (`two`) adds a second `fill` label (the `leadingIconDescription` field) and a second gap: the frame measures the smallest width at which the equal split gives each label its content, never below 96 nor above 136 (`Ok` and `Ok` give 100, `Open` and `Edit` give 133, `Settings` and `Ok` give 136, the cap). The widths in the MCP are the package's measurer's; in the app they differ by a few pixels with the system font (the minimum and the maximum do not).

**Setup.** Section 6 done (the test repository and `mapping-mcp.js`), R25.22 done (it builds `ROOT/m3-tokens`); the requests to the MCP go through the stdio client (appendix A). `ROOT` is the server's projects root (`design/mapeamentos`) and `REPO` the clone of the Mapping repository, where `scripts/testing/hug-fill.mjs` is (do not write a script in its place). The shell functions used to measure a PNG are `convert` calls written in the steps (no `tinta` or `medir`). In the `hug.png` crops below, the chip at `Y` 10, 60 and 110 is the band `400x40+0+Y`.

### R26 — Import the signature

**What it covers:** the Import the parameters by signature stage (S2): the MCP's `plan_signature_import` tool and the `planSignatureImport` importer, with **hand-written sheets** (`source.extractor: "agent"`, R26.1 to R26.8) and, in R26.9 to R26.12, with the sheet that the **Kotlin extractor** (`mapping-signature.js kotlin`, S3) writes: determinism, import with no error, ambiguous overload and errors; **R26.13 to R26.18** (S4) do the same with the **SwiftUI** (`swift`: explicit `init`, memberwise, `--init` and ambiguous `init`, the positional `#0` in `code.params`) and **Figma** (`figma`: the four natures, the `#id` suffix, the sheet linked in `sources` with `values`) extractors and check the errors and the options that each reader refuses; **R26.19** checks the SwiftUI reader on the `init`s of an `extension` (in the file and in an `--also` file) and inside `#if`, the memberwise listed as `0` next to an `extension` `init`, and the raw string `#"…"#` as a default. **R26.20** (stage #1926) checks that the Figma sheet's `ignore` in the type's `sources` is valid with the system **outside** `origins` (`validate_library`, `plan_signature_import`: `Icon` leaves `unmapped`) and that, without `signature`, it is refused with the message that names both ways out (`validate_specialization`). The preview writes nothing; the test script writes the response's `spec`, validates the library, reimports the same sheet (nothing changes), imports a **changed** sheet (new optional field, `removed`, updated default and no break) and checks the errors, including the `signatureFile` that is not `.json`. **Rule to check at the end:** no `plan_signature_import` call changes a file; only the helper's `gravar` writes.

**Setup.** Section 6 done (the test repository and `mapping-mcp.js`); the requests to the MCP are made by the stdio client (appendix A: `WS=<workspace> node scripts/testing/mcp-stdio-client.mjs calls.json > saida.txt`, one output per step's call, with `n` the number of the `plan_signature_import` response in the output). `ROOT` is the server's projects root (`design/mapeamentos` in section 6) and `REPO`, the Mapping repository. The `path` and `signatureFile` paths in the calls are **relative to `ROOT`**. `scripts/testing/assinatura.mjs` does what the agent does after the preview: `gravar <saida.txt> <package> <sheet.json> <specialization file> [n]` writes the response `n`'s `spec` and the sheet to `signaturePath`; `igual <saida.txt> <specialization file> [n]` says `equal` or `different`.

### R27 — Reading direction (RTL)

**What it covers:** the Reading direction stage (R1 onward, `formatVersion` 4 of the **component** and 2 of the icons file): the mirrored row, the logical anchors (`anchors.start`), `font.align` `start` (the new default), the `icon` node's `mirror` (by the set) and the `path` **without** `mirror`, the `{ "$direction": "rtl" }` condition and the subtree with a fixed `direction: "ltr"`. The steps check the validation (the new keys, the previous version and the combination errors) and the **drawing**, by probing pixels in the MCP's PNG and in the app's canvas crop. **Rule to check:** `mapping.json` stores nothing of the component's direction; it belongs to the library and to whoever instantiates. The project's and the container's, when pinned, are the only ones it stores (R27.11). R27.12 checks that the **measures** read the anchor and the direction: the size an anchored instance is created with, `fit_marking` and **Arrange** agree and follow the `$anchor.*` and `$direction` of `sizing`.

**Note on the instance's direction.** Steps R27.1 to R27.10 exercise the direction that the **component** pins (`"direction": "rtl"` on the template's root), which holds in the app, the MCP and the viewer with no parameter. The **instance's** direction (the project's and the container's, in the app and in `update_project`/`add_container`/`update_container`, and the `direction` of `render_container`/`render_marking`) is exercised in R27.11, with the test `spacer`, which pins none.

**Setup.** Section 6 done (the test repository and `mapping-mcp.js`); the requests to the MCP are made by the stdio client (appendix A: `WS=<workspace> node scripts/testing/mcp-stdio-client.mjs calls.json`; arguments from `[{"list":true}]`). `ROOT` is the server's projects root (`design/mapeamentos` in section 6) and `REPO` is the Mapping clone. The test library `m3-rtl` is a copy of the Material 3 (Compose) package in which the `node -e` below swaps **two** components (the `card`, 300 × 150, and the `spacer`, 100 × 30) and adds to the icon set the `proof` icon (`"mirror": true`, a rectangle on the **left half** of the `viewBox`, so the mirroring shows in the probe). The test `card` has, with `rtl` pinned on the root: the **row** (red 60, blue 40, green 20, `gap` 10) at y 10 to 30; the **text** `RTL` (`font.align` `start`) at y 40 to 60, in a `fill` box from x 10 to 290; the `none` **strip** at y 70 to 100, with the orange anchor (`anchors.start` 0), the `icon` node `proof` (`anchors.left` 10), the `path` node with the same drawing and **without** `mirror` (`anchors.left` 60) and the `$direction` condition's rectangle (`anchors.left` 110); and the **`fixed`** strip, with `direction: "ltr"`, at y 110 to 134 (a rectangle `anchors.start` 0, the same `icon` at `anchors.left` 60 and the text `LTR` at `anchors.left` 120). The test `spacer` **pins no direction**: a `row` (`gap` 0, `justify: start`) with a red (`B3261E`) 40 × 30 rectangle and a blue (`1565C0`) 40 × 30 one; it follows the container's direction in R27.11.

```bash
node -e '
const fs=require("fs");const L="ROOT/m3-rtl/";
const ic=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(L+"icons/material-icons.json","utf8"));
ic.formatVersion=2;ic.icons.proof={mirror:true,paths:[{d:"M0 0 L10 0 L10 24 L0 24 Z",fill:true}]};
fs.writeFileSync(L+"icons/material-icons.json",JSON.stringify(ic));
const r=(name,w,fill,extra)=>Object.assign({type:"rect",name,width:w,height:20,fill},extra||{});
const ico=(x)=>({type:"icon",name:"proof",width:24,height:24,color:"#4A148C",anchors:{left:x,top:0}});
const txt=(name,text,extra)=>Object.assign({type:"text",name,text,height:20,color:"#000000",font:{size:14,align:"start"}},extra);
const card={format:"mapping-component",formatVersion:4,id:"card",name:"Card",size:{width:300,height:150},
 template:{type:"frame",name:"root",direction:"rtl",fill:"#FFFFFF",layout:{type:"column",padding:10,gap:10},children:[
  {type:"frame",name:"lane",height:20,layout:{type:"row",gap:10},children:[r("r1",60,"#B3261E"),r("r2",40,"#1565C0"),r("r3",20,"#1B5E20")]},
  txt("label","RTL",{width:"fill"}),
  {type:"frame",name:"strip",height:30,layout:{type:"none"},children:[
    r("anchor",20,"#E65100",{anchors:{start:0,top:0}}),ico(10),
    {type:"path",name:"arrow",d:"M0 0 L10 0 L10 24 L0 24 Z",viewBox:[24,24],fill:"#00897B",width:24,height:24,anchors:{left:60,top:0}},
    r("condition",20,{"$if":{"$direction":"rtl"},then:"#F9A825",else:"#9E9E9E"},{anchors:{left:110,top:0}})]},
  {type:"frame",name:"fixed",direction:"ltr",height:24,layout:{type:"none"},children:[
    r("f1",30,"#B3261E",{anchors:{start:0,top:0}}),ico(60),txt("label2","LTR",{width:100,anchors:{left:120,top:0}})]}]}};
fs.writeFileSync(L+"components/card.json",JSON.stringify(card));
const sw=(name,fill)=>({type:"rect",name,width:40,height:30,fill});
const row={format:"mapping-component",formatVersion:4,id:"spacer",name:"Spacer",size:{width:100,height:30},
 template:{type:"frame",name:"row",layout:{type:"row",gap:0,justify:"start"},children:[sw("a","#B3261E"),sw("b","#1565C0")]}};
fs.writeFileSync(L+"components/spacer.json",JSON.stringify(row));
'
```

The step R27.12 adds its own type to a copy of the library (the `tipbox`: anchored at the root, its `sizing.width` by `$direction` and its `sizing.height` by `$anchor.side`), with the shell, in the folder that `cp -r ROOT/m3-rtl ROOT/m3-r27-12` created:

```bash
node -e '
const fs=require("fs");const L="ROOT/m3-r27-12/";
const tip={format:"mapping-component",formatVersion:4,id:"tipbox",name:"Tip box",size:{width:100,height:40},
 sizing:{width:{"$if":{"$direction":"rtl"},then:120,else:80},height:{"$switch":"$anchor.side",cases:{bottom:90},default:30}},
 anchor:{side:"bottom",align:"center",offset:{main:4,cross:0}},
 template:{type:"frame",name:"root",fill:"#1565C0",layout:{type:"none"}}};
fs.writeFileSync(L+"components/tipbox.json",JSON.stringify(tip));
const f=L+"material3-compose.spec.json",sp=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8"));
sp.layers[0].annotationTypes.push({id:"tipbox",name:"Tip box",component:"components/tipbox.json",fields:[]});
fs.writeFileSync(f,JSON.stringify(sp));
'
```

The drawing checks are pixel probes; define in the shell, once:

```bash
hex() { convert "$1" -format "%[hex:p{$2,$3}]\n" info:; }
tira() { convert "$1" -crop "$2" +repage -fuzz 25% -trim info: | awk '{print $3, $4}'; }
pto() { read X Y W _ <<<"$1"; awk -v x=$X -v y=$Y -v w=$W -v L=$2 -v u=$3 -v v=$4 'BEGIN{s=w/L;printf "%d %d\n", x+u*s, y+v*s}'; }
```

`hex <png> <x> <y>` prints the pixel's color; `tira <png> <WxH+X+Y>` crops the strip, removes the background and prints the ink's size and its box inside the crop (`WxH` and `<crop>+X+Y`); `pto "<data-selection-box>" <marking width in units> <u> <v>` converts a point in component units to the canvas crop's pixel (the selected marking; read the `.canvas-host`'s `data-selection-box` **before** `Esc`), for `hex`. In the MCP's PNG with `zoom` 1 and `padding` 0, 1 unit is 1 pixel.

**Spacer crop (R27.11).** When a step asks for `sp-<name>.png`: select the Spacer, frame it (`Shift+2`) and zoom (`Ctrl+=` on the canvas) until it is more than 300 px wide on screen (the same zoom in the three crops); read the `.canvas-host`'s `data-selection-box` (`sel`), press **Esc** and take the crop as in R27.9. The probes are `hex sp-<name>.png $(pto "$sel" 100 <u> 15)`; at 3 units or more from any edge.

| Step | Action | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R27.1 | **Build and validate the library.** In the shell, `cp -r REPO/libraries/material3-compose ROOT/m3-rtl` and run the Setup's `node -e`. ### R28 — Named slots

**What it covers:** the Named slots stage (#1080, `formatVersion` 17): the `slots` of a type (`id`, `name`, `description`, `accepts`, `max`) and `code.<platform>.slots`, how `validate_library` checks them against the component, and what they do in the drawing: each child is drawn in the box of **its** slot, the default content (`fallback`) of a **full** slot is absent and that of an **empty** one is present, moving a child to the other slot changes the drawing, and a child past the corner of a rounded, clipping slot is cut by it (decision 23). The app part also covers the pending item of a child in the **Details** (R28.19). The MCP part (R28.15 to R28.18): `create_marking` with `inside` + `slot`, the `slots` and `slot` of `get_marking` and `get_component`, and `get_code_hints` with each child in the argument of its slot.

**Setup.** Section 6 done (the test repository and `mapping-mcp.js`); the MCP requests go through the stdio client (appendix A: `WS=<workspace> node scripts/testing/mcp-stdio-client.mjs calls.json`). `ROOT` is the server's projects root (`design/mapeamentos` in section 6) and `REPO` is the clone of the Mapping repository. The test library is `REPO/tests/fixtures/slots/` (a `formatVersion` 17 specialization with three types: the **Bar** (`bar`, 360 × 56, with two slots: `navigationIcon`, a fixed 40 × 40 box that takes 1 `pin`, and `actions`, which takes 3; each has a default content, the text of `navLabel` or `actionLabel`), the **Pin** (`pin`, 24 × 24, a lilac circle `E8DEF8` with the text `pin`) and the **Rounded bar** (`rounded-bar`, 200 × 80, corner radius 16, clipping, with a single slot `content` that fills it). In the shell, define: `hex() { convert "$1" -format "%[hex:p{$2,$3}]\n" info:; }`.

**Documented differences (decision 24), not ❌:** (a) The **empty** slot appears filled only in the MCP's image (`render_container`, `render_marking`): the app's canvas shows the empty slot's default content too, but the box it draws for a slot with nothing in it is the probe's, so that box is not compared by pixel with the MCP's. (b) The label cut by the width, as in the `segmented-button` of the Material 3 library, differs: `S…` in the app and `…` in the MCP. Compare the app with the MCP only on the **children** (position and color) and the corner.
