```bash
xdotool windowactivate --sync $W
xdotool key --clearmodifiers ctrl+l
xdotool type --delay 20 "/absolute/path/file-or-folder"   # folder with "/" at the end
xdotool key --clearmodifiers alt+o
```

- **Recipe 5 (cloud), folder that has content** (seen in R0.7, when locating the folder of a project that already has `images/` and `specs/`): the GTK autocomplete list opens after typing the path (a "chromium" window in the `xdotool` list, about 48 px with one suggestion and 94 px with four) and `alt+o` does nothing. Here `Escape` **erases the path field**, and `Escape` + `alt+o` may open the parent directory (refused by Chrome, "contém arquivos do sistema"; its **Escolher uma pasta diferente** button reopens the picker).
- **Recipe 5 (cloud), sibling folders.** `selectFolder` already resolves the autocomplete list, even with similarly named folders (`migracao` next to `migracao10` to `migracao13`: the list reaches 94 px): it clears the field before typing, clicks **Open** and repeats the click on another point of the button while the list does not close; if it does not, the error says "autocomplete list open (sibling folders with the same start)".
- **Recipe 5 (cloud), folder that has content, workaround.** By hand: type the path, **click the GTK Open button** by coordinate (`xdotool mousemove X Y click 1`; the first click only closes the list and keeps the path) and then `alt+o`, checking the path in the field first. **No slash at the end of the path:** with it, the picker once resolved to a wrong subfolder (e.g. `specs/` inside the right folder) and the app asked "Create a project in this folder?" for it.

A pending permission prompt blocks the next picker: resolve it first.
- **Recipe 5 (cloud), focus:** `ctrl+l` and `xdotool type` go wherever the focus is. With the picker out of focus, they go to Chrome's address bar: activate the window with `xdotool windowactivate --sync $W` and check that `$W` is not empty before typing. The title of the **Open zip** picker is "Abrir arquivo" (singular), different from that of **Add images** ("Abrir arquivos").

Chrome shows "Permitir que este site edite arquivos?" with "Não permitir" (with focus) and "Permitir". Use `/usr/bin/python3.12` (the PATH's `python3` breaks `gi`). Expected output: `clicked Permitir press`; the `DeprecationWarning` is harmless.
- **Recipe 6 (cloud), continuation.** "no allow button" with the app already open means the browser already had the permission (reopening from **Recent projects** in the same Chrome run does not ask again): it is as much a success as clicking. To reopen from the recents, click the row's **Open <project name>** button (`getByRole('button', { name: 'Open <project name>', exact: true })`) and run the script.
- **Recipe 6 (cloud), read permission.** `allowPermission` also resolves "Permitir que este site veja e copie arquivos?" (read permission, e.g. when applying a specialization folder in R12.19); the buttons have the same names.

```python
import sys, gi
gi.require_version('Atspi', '2.0')
from gi.repository import Atspi
NAMES = ['Permitir em todas as visitas', 'Permitir', 'Allow on every visit', 'Allow']
found = []
def walk(n, d=0):
    if n is None or d > 60: return
    try:
        if n.get_role_name() == 'push button': found.append(n)
        for i in range(n.get_child_count()): walk(n.get_child_at_index(i), d + 1)
    except Exception: pass
desk = Atspi.get_desktop(0)
for i in range(desk.get_child_count()):
    app = desk.get_child_at_index(i)
    if app and 'hrom' in (app.get_name() or ''): walk(app)
by = {b.get_name(): b for b in found}
for want in NAMES:
    b = by.get(want)
    if b:
        ai = b.get_action_iface()
        names = [ai.get_action_name(k) for k in range(ai.get_n_actions())]
        k = next((k for k, x in enumerate(names) if x in ('press', 'click', 'doDefault', 'activate')), None)
        if k is None: print('no action', names); sys.exit(2)
        ai.do_action(k); print('clicked', want, names[k]); sys.exit(0)
print('no allow button'); sys.exit(1)
```

- **Working folder without accents:** `xdotool type` with accents was not tested; use paths without accents. With `LANGUAGE=pt_BR:pt` the app opens in pt-BR (the GTK picker stays in English).

**What the guide assumes of you.** You control Chrome through Playwright over CDP and have a **shell on the same computer** (the session's container). With the shell, you do the file operations outside the browser (create, copy, move, rename and unzip, read and rewrite `mapping.json`, change permissions in R6.8b, run the MCP) and all the **Disk** checks; that is why these steps are not [person].

- **"In a text editor next to it"** (R3.5, R6.3, R6.3b, R6.10): read and rewrite the file through the shell.
- **Deleting in the working folder** asks nothing (it is your container); even so, only delete inside `~/mapping-testes/`.

**Files and images.**

- **Paste** (R0.3 and others): fire a synthetic `paste` event with `DataTransfer` and the file on the page (click the canvas background first, outside the image). There is no system clipboard to put the file in.
- **Copy the reference** (R5.1): copy through the app (`Ctrl+C`) and read the text through the page (`navigator.clipboard.readText()`, with the `clipboard-read` permission granted by CDP) or through what the app shows. The scenario without `clipboard-read` (the copy bug's) is covered by the e2e `tests/e2e/folder.spec.ts` ("Details: copy reference with clipboard-write only asks no permission and writes the text").
- **Dragging** from the file manager is always [person] (there is no file manager). To add an image, use **Add images** through the real picker (cloud recipe 5) or the synthetic `paste`; `setInputFiles` only comes in as a last resort, by the prompt's "Never" rule.
- **Screenshot of `cadastro.png`** (R0): generate it with Chrome itself (full-page capture of `cadastro.html` at 1×) or with Playwright (`page.screenshot({ fullPage: true })`); the content is the same.
- **For "Update version…"** (R1.5): the native picker really opens; use cloud recipe 5.

**Interacting with the interface.**

- **Wait for the field to appear before typing.** After **+ Pair**, **+ Row**, **+ Entry**, choosing a type or opening a dialog, check that the field exists and has focus (or click it): what is typed before is lost. After typing, confirm with Enter.
- **Native dropdowns** (`<select>`): use `selectOption` by value or by label and check afterwards that no click landed on another control.
- **Zoom** (`Ctrl+=`, `Ctrl+-`, R1.20, R3.3): send the shortcut with `page.keyboard`; if the app does not react, fire the same `keydown` by script and record it in the report.
- **`Tab` in the note field:** if focus does not leave the `textarea` on the first send, send again or click outside (a component test proves the first `Tab` leaves and saves the note; not a finding).
- **Tooltips** do not come out in a screenshot: check the element's `title` attribute (or the `aria-label`, on icon buttons). The **Definition** row of Details has a `<span class="tooltip">` instead, read through the DOM.
- **Date in R1.8:** fill the date field's value with `YYYY-MM-DD` instead of using the picker.
- **Window:** Chrome comes up at 1600 × 1200 (recipe 2; viewport near 1600 × 1050); for R0.4b's narrow pass, resize through CDP (`Browser.setWindowBounds`) or with `xdotool windowsize`, and check the width with `innerWidth` immediately before the visual pass. If it does not resize, mark the narrow pass as "not executed (window did not resize; narrow layout covered by the e2e `narrowLayout.spec.ts`)".
- **Short notices** (e.g. "The review is back where you left off.", "2 change(s) accepted.") disappear in a few seconds: read the notice right after the action and, if you miss it, repeat the action before recording.
- **Review note field:** its accessible name is "Note for the agent"; on screen, it opens through the note button (tooltip "Add note") of the item's header or of a marker's frame, and saves when leaving the field (`Tab`), with no confirm button.
- **Destructive confirmations** (Delete project, container, marking or layer; "Close without saving?"; Remove a specialization; "References will break"): their `role` is `alertdialog`, not `dialog`, named by the title and described by the body. Check through the accessibility tree.
- **A single app tab.** Navigate the same tab with `page.goto`; an old Mapping tab may hold the project. Before each action that changes something, check that the tab's title is still the app's; if it changed, stop and reconnect through CDP. The decisions of a review in progress are saved in the proposal and come back with **Continue**. Reopening the project in a new tab **loses the undo history**: do not restart Chrome nor reload before the undo steps.
- **Window shortcuts with focus in a field:** before shortcuts such as `Ctrl+Shift+N`, `Ctrl+Shift+6`, `Shift+1` or `Shift+2`, take focus out of text or number fields (Esc or a click on the canvas): sending the shortcut may type the number in the field.
- **Window shortcuts through Playwright:** `page.keyboard.press('Control+Shift+1')` does not work (the `key` becomes `!`); use `Control+Shift+Digit<n>`. The shortcut **toggles** the window (open, it closes): to open or close safely use `openWindow(page, id)` and `closeWindow(page, id)` of `scripts/testing/cloud.mjs`, idempotent (they only click when the state is different; ids and shortcuts in the table below).

  Ids and shortcuts: `tree` 1, `layers` 2, `details` 3, `list` 4, `incomplete` 5, `diagnostics` 6, `proposals` 7, `notices` 8, `catalog` 9, `comments` 0 (all `Ctrl+Shift+<n>`).

- **Dragging and resizing the window:**
  - `drag(page, from, to, { select, steps, allowOffCanvas })` (points from `ponto`) throws, before moving the mouse, if `from` does not fall on the canvas (`allowOffCanvas: true` goes on) and warns when the click did not select anything. It also warns if `from` falls within the handle's radius (only the 4 corners, 12 to 22 px): start from the center of the marking.
  - `paletteDrag(page, type, to, { capture })` drags from the Palette and returns `{ via }` (`nativo` or `sintetico`). `setViewport(page, width, height)` puts the window at `innerWidth × innerHeight`: use it at 1280×720 and 900×720.
- **Locator that failed:** `cloud.mjs run` lists up to 10 candidates (role, name, region) after the error; outside it, `cloud.mjs find <text>`.

- **Export:** the app's "Export project" dialog stays open after the download; close it (**Cancel**) before the next step, or the app seems stuck.
- **Console:** register `page.on('console')` and `page.on('pageerror')` right when opening the page, before the first action (what came before is lost). Each script is a new process and `state()` does not read the console: register both listeners in every step script and print what comes after the `state()`.
- **Report:** save `relato.md` in the working folder at the end of each test script and, at closing, deliver it as a comment on the phase's sub-issue (`docs/TESTING-NUVEM.md`). It holds even if the round stops halfway.

**MCP.**

- **The MCP requests** are made by you, with the repository's minimal MCP client over stdio, [`scripts/testing/mcp-stdio-client.mjs`](../scripts/testing/mcp-stdio-client.mjs), against the commit's `dist-mcp/mapping-mcp.js` (cloud recipe 9). R3.6, R5.2 to R5.7, R9.13, R9.15, R9.19, R9.20, R9.24 to R9.28 and R12.20 become direct calls to the tools the step cites; R5.1 too: copy the reference through the app (`Ctrl+C`) and pass the text to `resolve`, which the copied reference has to resolve. **In the report, record that the requests were made over stdio.**
- **Roots of the stdio client:** with no arguments after `--` and no `MAPPING_MCP_ARGS`, the client reads the `.mcp.json` of the `WS` folder (`mcpServers.mapping.args`); without that file, or with it invalid, it uses the roots of `examples/workspace/`. The stderr says which source it used.
- **How to use the client:** `WS=<workspace> node scripts/testing/mcp-stdio-client.mjs calls.json`, with `calls.json` = `[{"list":true}]` (lists the tools and the schemas) or `[{"name":"<tool>","args":{...}}, ...]`. The server's arguments are those of the workspace's `.mcp.json`: the default is that of `examples/workspace/` (`tools/mapping-mcp.js --root projects --root specializations`); for others, pass them after `--` or in the `MAPPING_MCP_ARGS` variable (JSON). Assemble each tool's arguments from the schema.
- **The client's images:** tools that return an image (`get_marking_image`, `get_container_file`) save the file to `IMGDIR` (default: the current folder) with the extension by type and print `{ saved, mimeType }`; each response also carries `url`, which the client checks against the live server (valid only while it runs): the call's last item is the `urlCheck` (`head`, `get` and `sameAsImage`, the bytes of the `GET` against the image's). Look at the saved file and check the drawing.
- **Roots from R25.35 on:** `fiel-tk` and the other folders are outside the `.mcp.json` roots: start the server with `--root <working folder>` (`MAPPING_MCP_ARGS`).
- **Roots:** `add_container` (with `file`) and `apply_specialization` only read files inside the server's roots, which is why section 6 creates the `assets/` root (`--root assets`) with the screenshots and `sdui.json`. A file outside it gives `outside-roots`: copy it to `assets/`. With two roots, `create_project` without `root` answers `root-required` (R5.2 asks for the `design/mapeamentos` root). The `file` is relative to the root: `sdui.json`, not `assets/sdui.json`.
- **Check the `revision`:** before and after each tool, compare the `revision` and the content of `mapping.json`.

**Browser's prior state.** The round's Chrome profile is new (recipe 2). If you reuse one, record before R4.1 the home-screen projects and `localStorage.getItem('mapping.reviewResume')` (`file://` and `localhost` differ). Delete nothing.

**App version.** The tested app is the local build of the message's commit (recipe 1): check the build id in Settings › About. If it differs, stop: the build is stale. Never use an incognito window nor the preview, and never clear the site data.

## Appendix B — Disk operations by system

Do these operations with the project **closed** in the app, unless the step says otherwise.

**Moving, copying and renaming folders** (R0.7, R3, R6.7, R7.2): through the file manager or the terminal (`mv`, `cp -r` on macOS and Linux; `Move-Item`, `Copy-Item -Recurse` in PowerShell). In R7.2, delete the `backups/` folder of the copy (`rm -r principal-reparo/backups` or `Remove-Item -Recurse`).

**Removing the write permission** (R6.8b) and giving it back (R6.11):

| System | Remove | Give back |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS and Linux | `chmod a-w loja`, or in Finder: Get Info on the `loja` folder › Sharing & Permissions › your user to **Read only** (the **folder**, not the subfolders: the browser writes a new file and renames it over the old one, so a read-only `mapping.json` is not enough) | `chmod u+w loja`, or back to **Read & Write** in Finder |
| In the cloud (the session runs as `root`, and `chmod a-w` does not block its writing) | `chattr +i loja` (the **folder**, not the file; needs `root`) | `chattr -i loja` |
| Windows | `mapping.json` as Read-only in Properties, or `attrib +R loja\mapping.json` (in Git Bash, `chmod a-w mapping.json` turns on the same attribute) | uncheck it, or `attrib -R loja\mapping.json` |

**Editing `mapping.json` without write permission** (R6.10):

- macOS and Linux (and the cloud, with the immutable folder): the editor may not manage to save, because the folder is protected. Run, inside `loja`: `python3 -c "p='mapping.json';s=open(p).read().replace('Footer','External footer',1);f=open(p,'r+');f.write(s);f.truncate()"` (rewrites the file in place, without creating another).
- Windows: turn the attribute off only to edit and turn it back on right after saving (`attrib -R`, edit and save, `attrib +R`).

**Reading the `revision` without opening the editor:** `python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('mapping.json'))['revision'])"` (or `(Get-Content mapping.json | ConvertFrom-Json).revision` in PowerShell).
